## Responsibility

Owned behavior:

- implement pipeline phases 6-8: type checking, registration/cluster
  resolution, and overload resolution;
- consume `mizar_resolve::resolved_ast::ResolvedAst` plus
  `mizar_resolve::env::SymbolEnv` and produce `TypedAst`,
  `TypeFactTable`, `ResolutionTrace`, and `ResolvedTypedAst`;
- normalize soft type expressions into deterministic predicate-like forms;
- build layered checker-local typing contexts over resolver-owned symbol
  identities;
- infer term and formula types while preserving recoverable error state;
- record type facts, coercion candidates, and `InitialObligationId`-backed
  initial obligations without assigning `VcId`s;
- index pending and activated registrations, compute replayable cluster
  closure, apply reduction registrations with provenance, and detect bounded
  saturation failures;
- expand and filter overload candidates, select ordinary roots, join accepted
  same-root refinements, insert allowed `qua` views, and preserve failed sites;
- keep ids, debug renderings, diagnostics, fact queries, candidate order, trace
  order, and artifact-facing projections deterministic.

Out of scope:

- lexical, syntax, parser, frontend, module-index, source-loading, and package
  planning ownership;
- name lookup, import/export validation, label resolution, and signature
  collection, which remain owned by `mizar-resolve`;
- arbitrary first-order reasoning, ATP search, proof certificate acceptance,
  theorem validity checking, and kernel replay;
- `VcId` assignment, `ObligationAnchor` construction, VC generation, and proof
  policy decisions beyond emitting checker-local initial obligations;
- stable published artifact schemas, cache storage, LSP rendering, and build
  scheduling;
- activating unverified local registrations merely because they occur earlier
  in the same source pass.

Boundary rules:

- every checker fact must be explainable as a declared type predicate,
  checker-owned inference fact, or registration-derived fact with trace
  provenance;
- source behavior must follow `doc/spec/en/` and existing `.miz` test intent,
  not observed source convenience;
- recovered or erroneous nodes may receive partial typed output, but invalid
  facts must not be exported as verified metadata;
- active registrations used for automatic inference must come from accepted
  dependency artifacts or accepted local summaries; an interim policy may
  record pending/unverified registrations and generated obligations, but it
  must not make unverified registrations contribute automatic facts;
- no task may introduce proof search, hidden coercion insertion, unrecorded
  cluster facts, or return-type-based overload selection.

## Authority Order And Specification References

For language behavior, use the repository authority order:

1. `doc/spec/en/`
2. `tests/**/*.miz`
3. `tests/coverage/spec_trace.toml`
4. `tests/**/*.expect.toml`
5. `doc/design/`
6. `crates/`

| SSA-001 | `spec_gap` | Task 35 resolves constructor property arguments vs fields-only extensionality by adopting the fields-only constructor rule. Spec 05 and 07 now state that default constructors accept fields only, generate projection axioms only for fields, and leave property values to Chapter 7 property implementations. The inactive `advanced_semantics` seed `fail_structure_constructor_property_arg_001` and traceability rows `spec.en.05.structures.constructor_fields_only.semantic` / `spec.en.07.modes.property_implementation.not_constructor_source.semantic` pin the rejected constructor-property form until MC-G020/MC-G030 runner and payload gaps close. No checker/core source semantics changed. |
| SSA-002, SSA-011, SSA-012 | `spec_gap` | Task 36 resolves structure member identity, implicit upcast path uniqueness, and inheritance acyclicity. Spec 05 now tracks inherited member identity as root declaration plus inheritance path/view, requires exact parent-member coverage and per-parent type-inclusion obligations discharged by the existing `coherence` block, preserves renamed same-root paths as distinct views, and names `structures.inherit.cycle` for cyclic inheritance. Spec 19 now states that implicit upcast uniqueness is syntactic over resolved `inherit` declaration paths. The inactive `advanced_semantics` seed `fail_structure_inherit_duplicate_member_coverage_001` pins duplicate parent-member coverage; existing structure/overload seeds remain valid, and the template view-leak seed guards cross-view evidence. No renamed-view reject seed was added because renamed-view exposure remains positive behavior. No checker/core source semantics changed. |
| SSA-003, SSA-010, SSA-016, SSA-019 | `spec_gap` / editorial | Task 37 resolves overload tie-breaks, equivalent-root ambiguity, specificity preorder wording, and the duplicated §19.6.1 text. Spec 19 now compares instantiated concrete parameter vectors under the normal `⊑` preorder after template expansion; template declared constraint strictness is not a tie-breaker, non-template priority applies only to mutually equivalent concrete vectors, return type remains excluded, and ambiguity is a nonempty maximal-root set with more than one distinct ordinary root. Ordinary definitions with identical argument signatures are declaration conflicts regardless of return type. Architecture 05 and the checker overload design now match this rule. Inactive seeds `fail_overload_equivalent_roots_ambiguity_001`, `fail_overload_template_equivalent_roots_ambiguity_001`, and `fail_resolve_same_signature_same_return_conflict_001` pin ordinary/template-derived equivalent-root ambiguity and the same-return ordinary declaration-conflict rule; the last remains inactive until resolver declaration-symbol support grows beyond the current different-return diagnostic. Mizar-core task 26 / template-audit F7 records the separate Phase A omitted-template inference determinism rule. No checker/core/resolver source semantics changed. |
| SSA-004 | `spec_gap` | Task 38 resolves functorial-cluster `for` semantics. Spec 17 now treats the trailing `for` type expression as an applicability guard over the full known normalized result type, including parameters and attributes, and the coherence/FOL encoding includes that guard as a premise. Spec 16's proof-obligation summary and spec 23's registration-node discussion delegate the guarded functorial encoding to Chapter 17. The inactive seed `fail_cluster_functorial_for_guard_001` and traceability row `spec.en.17.clusters.functorial_for_guard.semantic` pin that a valid registration does not provide its consequent at same-radix use sites that lack the guarded attribute. No checker/core source semantics changed. |
| SSA-005 | `spec_gap` | Task 39 resolves property-implementation coherence. ## Crate Completion And Exit Criteria

Hard gates:

- every non-deferred task in [todo.md](./todo.md) is committed independently,
  with one task per commit;
- no blocking/high specification inconsistency remains;
- no implemented source behavior remains that is absent from `doc/spec/en` and
  tests; behavior that cannot be specified/tested yet must be excluded from the
  milestone scope or left unimplemented as a deferred design item;
- milestone-owned specification items have `.miz` coverage, task-local Rust
  tests, or explicit deferred reasons;
- existing `.miz` tests and expectations were not changed merely to match
  implementation behavior;
- design docs, English/Japanese companions, and source remain synchronized;
- checker crate boundaries are not violated;
- required verification commands pass or have explicit unrun justification;
- read-only crate quality review assigns at least 90/100 after hard gates pass.

Verification commands:

```text
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy -p mizar-checker --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p mizar-checker
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test
```

Additional commands are required for resolver boundary, corpus, or shared
harness tasks as noted in [todo.md](./todo.md).

Crate exit report:

- added [crate_exit_report.md](./crate_exit_report.md) and the Japanese
  companion at crate closeout;
- includes task commits, review results, verification, deferred items, external
  dependency gaps, quality score, and next-crate handoff.

## Task 248 Frozen Source/Binding-Context Producer Contract

Task 248 is the first executable producer in the accepted Task-247 graph. Its
canonical language authority is Chapters 04 §4.3 and §4.6, 11 §11.2, 12
§12.3 and §12.7, and 15 §15.10. The exact audit owners are MC-G011 and
MC-G016. This
task repairs a `test_gap` and two `source_drift` seams: the runner currently
flattens reserve items and loses per-item shell/order/context provenance, and
the final `TypedAst` / `ResolvedTypedAst` handoff does not retain the
declaration-to-`BindingEnv` identity checked separately by the runner. There is
no blocking `spec_gap`, `boundary_violation`, or `repo_metadata_conflict`.

The syntax-free checker input is frozen to:

- source/module identity and one module typed site;
- ordered resolver-shell projections containing opaque shell identity, shell
  ordinal, supported source-item role (`reserve` or definition block), range,
  parent, the exact source-shaped `Unspecified` visibility state, typed site,
  local lexical scope when the item opens a declaration context, and recovery
  state;
- ordered binding-site projections containing their owning shell, source
  ordinal, spelling, declaration and written-type ranges, typed site, and
  either a reserve-default role or a resolver-shaped definition-parameter
  `LocalTermBinding` identity.

The accepted cardinality and role sequence is also frozen to the named
smallest real consumer below: exactly one module reserve item with one reserve
binding, followed by exactly one definition block with one normal parameter
binding (or the same definition shell in the supported recovered-empty branch).
The Vec-based projection retains source order and an extension seam but does
not authorize broader shapes. Additional reserve items, including the
canonical distinct-name multiple-reserve form, are valid language shapes but
remain outside this exact Task 248 transaction and are rejected as
`UnsupportedTaskShape`. Separately, the replacement or duplicate rule for
re-reserving the same identifier is not defined by the cited canonical
chapters; that nonblocking `spec_gap` remains unresolved rather than acquiring
an implementation-defined meaning.

`mizar-test` retains all `SurfaceAst` inspection. It must match those projections
against the already collected `DeclarationShellSet` and derive the stable
lexical path from the exact source walk. `mizar-checker` receives no
`SurfaceNodeId`, `SyntaxKind`, or raw AST. It validates the payload, builds one
checker-owned `BindingEnv`, source-item/declaration tables, explicit
`BindingContextId` to `LocalTypeContextId` links, predecessor links, and the
reserve-default shadow relation. Same-scope duplicate local binders, missing or duplicate
rows/sites, reordered or stale ordinals, range/source/module mismatches,
wrong-role or partial payloads and any explicit/recovered visibility state
outside this task's `Unspecified` slice fail atomically. Recovery has exactly
two branches. A supported recovered shell with zero binding sites must produce
an incomplete producer result containing one explicit empty recovered context
and one deterministic internal recovery diagnostic; the complete-handoff
assembler must reject that result before installing any `TypedAst` or
`ResolvedTypedAst` table. A recovered shell with any claimed binding site must
fail atomically before publishing even the incomplete result. Neither branch
fabricates a binder.

The immutable handoff is stored in `TypedAst`. `ResolvedTypedAst` copies it
only from that typed AST and has no separately replaceable runner input.
Nonempty debug rendering is deterministic; empty handoffs preserve existing
debug bytes. Public access is borrowed/read-only so future Core Task 33 can
consume the final checker-owned table rather than runner-built seeds.

The smallest real Task-10 consumer is the new spec-derived pass fixture
`tests/miz/pass/types/pass_type_elaboration_source_binding_context_shadowing_001.miz`
with the exact source below and one matching `type_elaboration` sidecar:

```mizar
reserve x for set;
definition
  let x be set;
end;
```

It contains one top-level builtin-`set` reserve and one definition block whose
`set`-typed parameter has the same display spelling. It proves exact source
item order, distinct reserve/local binding identities, the local declaration
context, the local row's structural shadow link to the still-visible outer
reserve, the module context's retained reserve binding, lookup-readiness for
both contexts, declaration-to-binding/context/site links, and final
`TypedAst`-to-`ResolvedTypedAst` preservation. It asserts zero normalized type
results, RHS results, facts, obligations, formulas, proof payloads, or term-use
lookup sites. In particular, the real consumer does not claim that either
binding was selected for a source term; Tasks 252+ retain that ownership.
Recovery is covered by checker/runner corruption tests rather than a new
semantic fail fixture or an expectation rebaseline. The existing multi-reserve
pass remains an unchanged regression control.

Tests must cover success and real-source consumption plus the following exact
corruption matrix: missing and duplicate shell rows; missing and duplicate
binding sites; shell and binding-site reorder; stale shell and
visible-after-binding ordinals; declaration, written-type, and shell range
mismatches; source and module mismatches; parent/context and typed-site
mismatches; stale `LocalTermScope` / `LocalTermBinding` provenance; reserve and
definition-parameter role swap; same-scope duplicate local binder; unsupported visibility;
recovered-empty/incomplete and recovered-with-binding branches; partial bundle;
and atomic non-publication. Determinism coverage must prove that two identical
runs yield identical ids, tables, and nonempty debug text; reordered input is
rejected rather than sorted; empty debug bytes remain unchanged; and
`ResolvedTypedAst` can only copy the `TypedAst`-owned complete table. Add

expectation, trace row, coverage status, count, or hash. The executable absence
remains a `test_gap`; the missing complete argument, `qua`, and final-handoff
seams remain `source_drift`. There is no blocking `spec_gap`,

`boundary_violation`, or `repo_metadata_conflict`.

5.6, Chapter 7 §§7.2-7.3 and 7.6, Chapter 8 §§8.1 and 8.3, Chapter 12
§§12.3, 12.5, 12.6.1, and 12.7, Chapter 18 §§18.1 and 18.2.2, and the
Appendix A type-expression grammar. The selected audit slices are MC-G014,

symbol/provenance data is authenticated input, and the real `mizar-test`

## Task 251 Frozen Source-Evidence Contract

Task 251 owns syntax-free transport of source-derived evidence requests and
externally supplied dependency references. Its exact canonical authority is
Chapter 03 §§3.2-3.6; Chapter 05 §§5.3-5.5; Chapter 06 §§6.2-6.5;
Chapter 07 §§7.2-7.3 and §§7.8-7.8.1; Chapter 08 §§8.1-8.3;
Chapter 13 §§13.4.2, 13.5, and 13.6; Chapter 17 §§17.1, 17.3.4, and
17.7-17.8; and Chapter 19 §§19.2.1-19.2.2, 19.4.2, and 19.6.2, with audit
slices MC-G016, MC-G018, and MC-G026.
This documentation prerequisite repairs the missing exact contract
(`design_drift`) only. The absent executable handoff remains `source_drift`
and its missing executable coverage remains `test_gap`; there is no blocking
`spec_gap`.

The public `source_evidence` module has two dense immutable tables.
`SourceEvidenceRequestId` identifies a `SourceEvidenceRequest` row containing
the typed owner and site, source range and ordinal, recovery state, request
kind, transport state, and authenticated origin.
The matching fields of `SourceEvidenceRequestInput` are exactly
`owner: TypedSiteRef`, `site: TypedSiteRef`, `source_range: SourceRange`,
`source_ordinal: usize`, `recovery: SourceEvidenceRecovery`,
`kind: SourceEvidenceRequestKind`, `state: SourceEvidenceInputState`, and
`origin: SourceEvidenceRequestOrigin`; source and module identity remain the
single transaction-level fields of `SourceEvidenceHandoffInput`.
`SourceEvidenceResponseId` identifies an ordered `SourceEvidenceResponse` row
belonging to one request. The matching public input DTOs are
`SourceEvidenceRequestInput` and `SourceEvidenceResponseInput`;
`SourceEvidenceHandoffInput` owns their vectors, `SourceEvidenceProducer`
validates them, and `SourceEvidenceHandoff` is the immutable result.
`SourceEvidenceError` is the atomic build/install error vocabulary.
`SourceEvidenceResponseKey` is the public opaque nonempty upstream response
identity; it carries no status by itself.
`SourceEvidenceDependencyCatalog` is the public input-only authentication
table keyed by that identity. Its `SourceEvidenceDependencyRecord` values
carry the key, an authenticated `request: SourceEvidenceRequestId` locator,
disposition, provenance, and optional payload; the catalog is validated but
is not copied wholesale into the handoff.
All schema types named in this section are public and syntax-free; immutable
output rows expose read-only accessors.

`SourceEvidenceRequestKind`, `SourceEvidenceInputState`,
`SourceEvidenceRequestOrigin`, `SourceEvidenceResponseDisposition`,
`SourceEvidenceResponsePayload`, `SourceEvidenceResponseProvenance`,
`SourceEvidenceRecovery`, and `SourceEvidenceError` are public
`#[non_exhaustive]` enums. Public request kinds are
`ModeExpansion`, `StructureInhabitation`, `AttributedTypeInhabitation`, `Sethood`,
`NonEmptiness`, `InheritancePath`, and `CoercionViability`. The current
implementation slice emits only the first three; the other variants freeze
the vocabulary used by the later source owners named below.
`StructureInhabitation` is the transport umbrella for the Chapter-17
base-shape and constructor-witness dependencies; it is not a claim that either
dependency is present or accepted.
The exact remaining variants are
`SourceEvidenceInputState::{Requested, Missing, Rejected, Supplied}`,
`SourceEvidenceResponseDisposition::{Rejected, Supplied}`,
`SourceEvidenceResponseProvenance::{ExplicitInput, ExternalDependency}`,
`SourceEvidenceRecovery::{Normal, Degraded}`, and
`SourceEvidenceRequestOrigin::SourceTypeApplication { application, expression,
attribute_chain }`, where `attribute_chain` is optional.

Transport states are `Requested`, `Missing`, `Rejected`, and `Supplied`.
They are not semantic results:

- `Requested` means that the checker need was recorded but no dependency
  lookup response was attached.
- `Missing` means only that the caller records a completed lookup and its
  supplied dependency bundle contains no input for the request. It does not
  assert semantic nonexistence.
- `Rejected` means that an authenticated upstream response explicitly marks
  its input rejected. Invalid Task-251 bundles are producer errors and must
  never be converted into this state.
- `Supplied` means only that one or more authenticated input references were
  transported. This disposition alone does not mean true, accepted, visible,
  consumable, satisfied, or proved; a later semantic owner must independently
  validate the referent and its status.

`Requested` and `Missing` have no response row. `Rejected` has exactly one
response row with `SourceEvidenceResponseDisposition::Rejected`, an opaque
nonempty upstream response identity, and authenticated response provenance,
but no response payload. `Supplied` has one or more rows with
`SourceEvidenceResponseDisposition::Supplied`, response identity/provenance,
and a payload. The exact initial `SourceEvidenceResponsePayload` variants are
`ModeExpansion(ModeExpansion)`,
`StructureBaseEvidence(ExistentialGateBaseEvidence)`,
`ExistentialGate(ExistentialGateInput)`, and `TypeFact(TypeFactId)`.
The first two are explicit dependency inputs, not accepted results. The
provenance vocabulary distinguishes only explicit caller-supplied input from
an authenticated external dependency input; tests use the semantics-neutral
`ExplicitInput` variant. It grants no semantic status.

Task 251 validates table identity, parentage, order, source/module/site/range/
recovery, response identity/provenance, reference existence, disposition/
payload/state cardinality, and duplicates before atomic publication. It never
evaluates an existential gate, interprets a fact, manufactures a normalized
pattern/trigger, or publishes evidence, truth, acceptance, or a checker
result. For an attributed request, its `SourceEvidenceRequestId` is the
opaque existential-gate request identity. Any later supplied
`ExistentialGateInput` is wrapped by the parent `SourceEvidenceResponseInput`;
the existing gate DTO gains no Task-251 field. The wrapper maps it back to the
request identity, and the producer authenticates the same owner/site/range,
Task-249 expression, and Task-250 chain.

`SourceEvidenceProducer::build` consumes the handoff input, the authenticated
Task-249 handoff, an optional authenticated Task-250 handoff, the existing
resolver-authenticated `SymbolEnv`, the existing `TypeFactTable`, and a
`SourceEvidenceDependencyCatalog`. `SymbolEnv` is used only to authenticate
the already-resolved Task-249 symbol head as `Mode` or `Structure`; it adds no
syntax or semantic result to the handoff. A response input contains only its
parent request, ordinal, and `SourceEvidenceResponseKey`; the producer
resolves that key in the catalog, requires the record's request locator to
equal the response parent, and publishes the matched
disposition/provenance/payload snapshot. Each catalog key must be nonempty
and unique, each response may consume its key exactly once, and every catalog
record must be consumed exactly once. Thus a missing key, duplicate reuse,
cross-request locator, or unconsumed stale record is an atomic
`SourceEvidenceError`, not a `Rejected` request. The exact real routes pass an
empty catalog.

`SourceEvidenceRequestOrigin` initially links one exact Task-249
`SourceTypeApplicationId` and `SourceTypeExpressionId`, with an optional
Task-250 `SourceAttributeChainId`. A mode or structure request requires the
matching Task-249 rows. An attributed request additionally requires the
matching Task-250 chain. The association is exact:

- for an application without an attribute chain, `expression` is the
  application's root, `owner` is `expression.site()`, `site` is
  `expression.head_site()`, `source_range` is
  `expression.source_range()`, and `source_ordinal` is
  `application.source_ordinal()`; request recovery is mapped from
  `expression.recovery()`; a builtin set/object head emits no request,
  while an authenticated `SymbolKind::Mode` or `SymbolKind::Structure` emits
  `ModeExpansion` or `StructureInhabitation`, respectively;
- for an attributed application, `expression` is again the application root,
  the chain must name that expression, `owner` is `expression.site()`, `site`

## Task 252 Frozen Primary-Term Producer Contract

This section is the independent documentation prerequisite for Task 252. It
repairs the missing exact contract (`design_drift`) only. The executable
primary-term handoff remains `source_drift`, and its missing producer,
corruption, and final-handoff coverage remains `test_gap` until the separate
implementation commit. Canonical Chapters 04 §§4.1-4.3, 4.4.1, and 4.6 and 13
§§13.1, 13.8.1-13.8.2, and 13.8.8 are sufficient; there is no blocking
`spec_gap`. MC-G017 and MC-G020 are the selected audit slices, Tasks 248-251
are dependencies, and the existing `mizar-test` Task-10 type-elaboration
runner is the consumer.

Task 252 must add a public, syntax-free `source_term` module with three dense,
immutable tables. The exact transaction input is:

```text
SourcePrimaryTermHandoffInput {
    source_id: SourceId,
    module_id: ModuleId,
    terms: Vec<SourcePrimaryTermInput>,
    references: Vec<SourcePrimaryTermReferenceInput>,
    numeric_type_requests: Vec<SourceNumericTypeRequestInput>,
}
SourcePrimaryTermInput {
    site: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    source_ordinal: usize,
    context: BindingContextId,
    recovery: SourcePrimaryTermRecovery,
    spelling: String,
    kind: SourcePrimaryTermKind,
    role: SourcePrimaryTermRole,
    parent: Option<SourcePrimaryTermId>,
}
SourcePrimaryTermReferenceInput {
    term: SourcePrimaryTermId,
    binding: BindingId,
    role: SourcePrimaryTermReferenceRole,
}
SourceNumericTypeRequestInput {
    term: SourcePrimaryTermId,
    owner: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    spelling: String,
    request_ordinal: usize,
}
```

`SourcePrimaryTermId`, `SourcePrimaryTermReferenceId`, and
`SourceNumericTypeRequestId` are dense zero-based row indices with public
`new(index)` and `index()` accessors. `LocalTermScope` is the existing
`mizar_resolve::names::LocalTermScope`. The validated output's exact private
fields are `SourcePrimaryTermHandoff { source_id: SourceId, module_id:
ModuleId, terms: SourcePrimaryTermTable, references:
SourcePrimaryTermReferenceTable, numeric_type_requests:
SourceNumericTypeRequestTable }`; its row types are
`SourcePrimaryTerm`, `SourcePrimaryTermReference`, and
`SourceNumericTypeRequest`, and its table types are
`SourcePrimaryTermTable`, `SourcePrimaryTermReferenceTable`, and
`SourceNumericTypeRequestTable`. The handoff exposes
`source_id() -> SourceId`, `module_id() -> &ModuleId`,
`terms() -> &SourcePrimaryTermTable`,
`references() -> &SourcePrimaryTermReferenceTable`,
`numeric_type_requests() -> &SourceNumericTypeRequestTable`, and
deterministic `debug_text() -> String` accessors. Each table exposes
only `get(id)`, source-ordered `iter()`, `len()`, and `is_empty()`, and each
term/numeric-request row exposes read-only accessors matching every input
field. A validated `SourcePrimaryTermReference` has exact private fields
`term: SourcePrimaryTermId`, `binding: BindingId`, `role:
SourcePrimaryTermReferenceRole`, `lexical_scope: Option<LocalTermScope>`, and
`use_ordinal: usize`; the last two are producer-derived output exposed as
`lexical_scope() -> Option<&LocalTermScope>` and `use_ordinal() -> usize`,
not caller-supplied input. There are no public
mutable or unchecked constructors. `SourcePrimaryTermProducer` validates the
complete input and returns the handoff. All public enums and the atomic
`SourcePrimaryTermError` are `#[non_exhaustive]`.

The exact initial kind vocabulary is `VariableReference`,
`ConstantReference`, `It`, `Numeral`, and `Parenthesized`.
`SourcePrimaryTermRecovery` is `Normal` or `Degraded`.
`SourcePrimaryTermRole` is `Value` or `CurrentDefinitionResult`; only `It`
uses the latter. `SourcePrimaryTermReferenceRole` is `Variable` or
`LocalConstant`. Variable rows accept only existing variable-like binding
kinds (`ReservedVariable`, `LetBinding`, `QuantifierBinder`, or
`DefinitionParameter`); local-constant rows accept only
`BindingKind::LocalAbbreviation`. A reference row is required exactly once
for a variable or constant and forbidden for `it`, numerals, and parentheses.
This distinct source kind does not widen the legacy semantic `TermKind`:
until a later consumer needs a distinction, both authenticated binding
references may still enter `TermFormulaChecker` as `TermKind::Variable`.

Every term `site` is `TypedSiteRef::Node` and names a unique arena node whose
`SourceAnchor::Range` equals `source_range`. The exact typed-node kind keys
are `source.term.variable-reference`, `source.term.constant-reference`,
`source.term.it`, `source.term.numeral`, and
`source.term.parenthesized`, respectively. `Normal` requires
`TypedNode::recovery == NodeRecoveryState::Normal`; `Degraded` requires
`Recovered` or `Degraded`, and no cross-mapping is accepted. The arena node's
typing state and semantic links remain legacy-consumer output and are not
Task-252 acceptance evidence.

`spelling` is the private extractor's deterministic token spelling, with
tokens separated by one ASCII space rather than a byte-for-byte source slice.
A reference spelling is a nonempty identifier spelling and must equal its
authenticated binding spelling; `It` is exactly `it`; a numeral is one or
more ASCII digits; and a parenthesized spelling is exactly
`format!("( {} )", child.spelling)`. Thus the producer can revalidate every
spelling without raw syntax.
Every term context must exist in `BindingEnv`. Variable, constant, `it`, and
numeral rows are roots unless wrapped by an eligible parenthesis; a
parenthesized row and its immediate child must have the same context. The
parent relation cannot cross contexts, and context existence alone grants no
binding-reference acceptance.

Rows are source ordered. `source_ordinal` is the dense zero-based pre-order
ordinal of the term table and therefore equals the row id/index; a wrapper
precedes its child, and roots and siblings retain source order. It is
independent of a reference's binding-event `use_ordinal`. A parent link is
absent for a root or names an earlier `Parenthesized` row whose range strictly
contains the child. Every parenthesized row owns exactly one immediate child,
no other row owns a child, and every non-root has exactly one parent. Thus
nested parentheses form a dense acyclic pre-order tree.

The initial graph is an eligible Task-252 closure, not an arbitrary term
graph. A `Parenthesized` row may be emitted only when its immediate semantic
child and every nested descendant are one of the five Task-252 kinds.
Parentheses whose closure contains an application, structure term, set,
choice, comprehension, `qua`, or another later-family term are not emitted by
Task 252, and Task 252 does not publish descendants from that mixed-family
subtree as detached roots. Tasks 253-255 must freeze their own cross-family
edge/origin schema before composing those terms; they may not reinterpret the
transparency defined here. Because the public five-kind input cannot describe
an omitted later-family node, the private extractor owns this whole-subtree
exclusion and its runner tests. The public producer proves only that every
supplied parent/child edge is closed within the five-kind table. Eligible
parentheses retain their own source site/range and child relation, but Chapter
13.1.3/13.8.8 remains transparent: a wrapper
creates no independent normalized type, expected-type entry, fact, axiom,
checked semantic term, or FOL node. The existing inner term identity and type
result are reused by legacy consumers.

Every numeral has exactly one numeric-type request, and no other kind has
one. Its term id, owner site, range, and spelling must equal the numeral row,
and request ordinals are dense in numeral source order. The request records
the missing external numeric-type dependency only;
Task 252 defines no response/result DTO, chooses no builtin `Nat` symbol,
normalizes no numeric type, and publishes no arithmetic or theorem fact. The
existing `TermFormulaChecker` numeric-gap diagnostic therefore remains the
semantic boundary. `it` records the source role only. Authenticating the
enclosing `func ... means` or `property ... means` owner and supplying its
current result type belongs to Tasks 260 and 264 respectively; Task 252 must
not fabricate either. A local-constant source
reference may be accepted only when an authenticated
`LocalAbbreviation` binding is supplied. Producing a `set`-style
`LocalAbbreviation` remains Task 269; any additional local-constant binding
role must be frozen by that owner rather than inferred by Task 252.

`SourcePrimaryTermProducer::build(
SourcePrimaryTermHandoffInput, &BindingEnv, &TypedArena
) -> Result<SourcePrimaryTermHandoff, SourcePrimaryTermError>` authenticates
source/module identity, typed-arena sites, ranges, spelling, recovery, dense
source order, kind/role/reference cardinality, parent
containment/ownership within the five-kind public graph, and numeral-request
cardinality before atomic publication.

For every reference row, the producer obtains `lexical_scope` only by cloning
`binding_env.contexts().get(term.context).lexical_scope`; callers cannot
supply or override it. It derives `use_ordinal` as the number of binding-table
rows whose declaration ranges end no later than the reference term's start;
previous use sites do not change this binding-event ordinal. This preserves
Task-248 `visible_after_ordinal` semantics when uses and later declarations
interleave and prevents a caller from moving a forward reference past its
declaration.

The dense binding table must be grouped in source order. Distinct declaration
groups have nonempty, nonoverlapping, strictly increasing ranges, and a
normal singleton group's `visible_after_ordinal` equals its binding id/index.
Consecutive rows may share the same declaration range only as an exact
duplicate-priority group. Every row in that group has the same spelling,
binding kind, owner context, and `BinderIdentity`, and the group's shared
`visible_after_ordinal` equals its final row's binding id/index. The whole
group therefore becomes visible only after its declaration event completes
and remains an equal-priority set through event validation, so
`BindingEnv::lookup` can return `Ambiguous`, which the producer rejects.
Reference rows follow their terms' source order and are pairwise
nonoverlapping. Cross-source, empty, reordered, partially overlapping, or
otherwise ordinal-incoherent events are rejected. The producer then
constructs exactly
`BindingLookupSite::new(term.spelling, term.context, derived_scope,
derived_use_ordinal)`, calls `BindingEnv::lookup`, and requires the result to
be exactly `BindingLookupResult::Local(reference.binding)` with that binding's
declaration range ending no later than the term start.
Every reachable non-local result (`Ambiguous`, `ForwardReference`,
`MissingExternalPayload`, or `Unresolved`), a different local winner, and any
lookup error are rejected before binding-kind/role validation.
`BindingLookupSite::new` carries no resolver payload, so `Resolver` is
structurally unreachable in Task 252; the producer nevertheless uses a
catch-all non-local rejection rather than accepting it if upstream behavior
later changes. The derived scope/order are stored in the immutable reference
row. This makes the lexical shadow winner and forward-reference boundary
authoritative rather than treating every context-visible binding as usable.

The producer never sorts, repairs, infers a binding, guesses an `it` owner,
or publishes partial output. `TypedAst` owns
`Option<SourcePrimaryTermHandoff>` and validates installation;
`ResolvedTypedAst` only clone-preserves it. Raw `SurfaceAst`,
`SurfaceNodeId`, and syntax kinds remain in one private
`mizar-test::runner::type_elaboration::source_term` leaf. The leaf may reuse
the current exact numeral, reserve-reference, and parenthesized-term helpers,
but must not duplicate or widen their legacy semantic/formula selectors.

### Exact Real Consumers And Oracles

Task 252 adds no `.miz` source. Its exact real selector contains only:

This section is the independent documentation prerequisite for Task 253. It
repairs the missing exact contract (`design_drift`) only. The executable

module-local consumer plus producer, corruption, and final-handoff coverage

10, 13 §13.2, 15 §15.2.3, and 19 provide sufficient source intent; there is no

248-252 are dependencies, and the existing `mizar-test` Task-10
type-elaboration runner is the consumer.

Task 253 must add a public, syntax-free `source_application` module with five
dense, immutable tables. The exact transaction input is:

```text
SourceFunctorApplicationHandoffInput {
    source_id: SourceId,
    module_id: ModuleId,
    applications: Vec<SourceFunctorApplicationInput>,
    wrappers: Vec<SourceFunctorWrapperInput>,
    candidates: Vec<SourceFunctorCandidateInput>,
    arguments: Vec<SourceFunctorArgumentInput>,
    type_requests: Vec<SourceFunctorTypeRequestInput>,
}
SourceFunctorApplicationInput {
    site: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    source_ordinal: usize,
    context: BindingContextId,
    recovery: SourceFunctorApplicationRecovery,
    spelling: String,
    kind: SourceFunctorApplicationKind,
    form: SourceFunctorApplicationForm,
    head_ordinal: usize,
    head: SourceFunctorHeadSite,
}
SourceFunctorWrapperInput {
    application: SourceFunctorApplicationId,
    ordinal: usize,
    site: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    context: BindingContextId,
    spelling: String,
    recovery: SourceFunctorApplicationRecovery,
}
SourceFunctorCandidateInput {
    application: SourceFunctorApplicationId,
    ordinal: usize,
    symbol: SymbolId,
    contribution: SourceContributionId,
}
SourceFunctorArgumentInput {
    application: SourceFunctorApplicationId,
    ordinal: usize,
    target: SourceFunctorArgumentTarget,
}
SourceFunctorTypeRequestInput {
    application: SourceFunctorApplicationId,
    candidate: Option<SourceFunctorCandidateId>,
    request_ordinal: usize,
    kind: SourceFunctorTypeRequestKind,
}
```

`SourceFunctorApplicationId`, `SourceFunctorWrapperId`,
`SourceFunctorCandidateId`, `SourceFunctorArgumentId`, and
`SourceFunctorTypeRequestId` are dense zero-based row indices with public
`new(index)` and `index()` accessors. The validated output's exact private
fields are `SourceFunctorApplicationHandoff { source_id, module_id,
primary_term_fingerprint, applications, wrappers, candidates, arguments,
type_requests }`, with one
table type and one immutable row type corresponding to each input vector.
Every table exposes only `get(id)`, source-ordered `iter()`, `len()`, and
`is_empty()`. Rows expose read-only accessors for their validated fields.
Candidate output additionally clones the producer-authenticated
`SemanticOrigin`, `Visibility`, `ExportStatus`, and
`Option<SignatureShell>` from `SymbolEnv`; callers cannot supply or override
them. `primary_term_fingerprint: String` is producer-derived as the exact
deterministic Task-252 `debug_text()` used at build time. It authenticates the
linked dependency without reowning or copying its rows and is not caller
input. The handoff exposes source/module/table accessors and deterministic
`debug_text()`. There are no public mutable or unchecked constructors.
`SourceFunctorApplicationProducer` validates the complete transaction before
publication. All public enums and the atomic `SourceFunctorApplicationError`
are `#[non_exhaustive]`.

`SourceFunctorApplicationKind` is `Symbolic` or `Inline`.
`SourceFunctorApplicationRecovery` is `Normal` or `Degraded`.
The exact source-shape forms are `Bare`, `Prefix`, `Infix`, `Postfix`,
`Bracket`, and `Functional`. This vocabulary distinguishes punctuation and
head position only; it does not create a semantic functor category beyond
Chapter 13.2. `Bare` has zero arguments, unparenthesized `Prefix` and
`Postfix` have exactly one, `Infix` has exactly two, `Bracket` has at least
one, and `Functional` has a parenthesized argument list. A symbolic
`Functional` application has at least one argument, while an inline
`Functional` application may have zero or more and always retains its
mandatory parentheses. `Symbolic` accepts all six forms; `Inline` accepts
only `Functional`. `head_ordinal` is zero for `Bare`, `Prefix`,
`Functional`, and `Bracket`, one for `Infix`, and the argument count for
`Postfix`; it preserves written left/right loci without assigning semantics.

`SourceFunctorHeadSite` is exactly:

```text
Single {
    site: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    spelling: String,
}
Paired {
    left_site: TypedSiteRef,
    left_range: SourceRange,
    left_spelling: String,
    right_site: TypedSiteRef,
    right_range: SourceRange,
    right_spelling: String,
}
```

Single heads are used by bare, prefix, infix, postfix, functional, and inline
shapes; paired heads are used only by bracket notation. Application, head,
and wrapper sites are distinct `TypedSiteRef::Node` arena nodes with exact
source anchors. The application kind key is exactly
`source.term.functor-application.symbolic` or
`source.term.functor-application.inline`; single and paired head sites use
`source.term.functor-head.single` and
`source.term.functor-head.bracket`; wrappers use
`source.term.functor-application.parenthesized`. Normal/degraded input must
exactly match the arena recovery state. Spelling is the private extractor's
deterministic token spelling with tokens separated by one ASCII space. The
producer revalidates the head positions, delimiters, argument
order/cardinality, and canonical whole-application spelling for the selected
form without receiving raw syntax.

Application rows use dense zero-based source pre-order:
`source_ordinal == SourceFunctorApplicationId::index()`. An outer application
precedes a nested application. Application, wrapper, candidate, argument, and
request rows are grouped in application order; their per-application ordinals
are dense and supplied order is never sorted or repaired. Every context must
exist in `BindingEnv`. Ranges are nonempty, belong to the transaction source,
have the required containment relation, and preserve effective source order.
No site, head site, wrapper site, argument occurrence, or candidate reference
may be duplicated.

`SourceFunctorArgumentTarget` is exactly
`Primary(SourcePrimaryTermId)` or
`Application(SourceFunctorApplicationId)`. The producer receives the
Task-252 `SourcePrimaryTermHandoff` and requires equal source/module identity.
A primary target must exist, share the application's binding context, itself
be a Task-252 root row (`parent() == None`), and have its range strictly
inside the parent application. Supplying an inner descendant ID is rejected. A nested
application target must name a later pre-order row in the same context and
have exactly one incoming argument edge. A Task-253 application's effective
range and spelling are its outermost wrapper when present and its application
row otherwise; a primary target retains its Task-252 root range/spelling,
including an eligible primary-only wrapper. Both target kinds use that
effective range for strict parent containment, argument-ordinal source order,
and sibling non-overlap. Each argument occurrence is owned exactly once.
Task 252 retains occurrence, spelling, range, binding, and numeric-request
ownership; Task 253 owns only application-to-child identity and order. It
must not copy a primary row or assign a second Task-252-style ID. Structure,
set, comprehension, choice, `qua`, and other
Task-254/255 targets are excluded whole-subtree until their owners freeze a
cross-family edge. If any direct or transitive argument belongs to an
unowned family, the containing application and its complete subtree emit no
Task-253 row; only unrelated eligible sibling application roots may publish.
The producer never publishes a partial argument list.

A `SourceFunctorWrapper` is the Task-253-owned cross-family transparent origin
for parentheses around an application. Wrapper ordinals are outer-to-inner,
all wrappers share the application's context, ranges strictly nest, and the
innermost range strictly contains the application. Its canonical spelling is
`format!("( {} )", contained_spelling)`, recursively. A wrapper creates no
primary term, semantic term/type, fact, axiom, or FOL node.
In particular, the existing `(1 ++ 2)` route publishes one Task-253 wrapper;
it must not fabricate a Task-252 `Parenthesized` row or detached Task-252
descendants, because Task 252 deliberately excludes parentheses whose closure
contains a later-family term.

Every symbolic candidate row is an individually authenticated resolver
functor reference attached to an application, not an authenticated
candidate-to-form association or an exhaustive/viable overload set. The producer resolves
the exact `SymbolEntry`, requires `SymbolKind::Functor`, verifies its
`SourceContributionId`, cloned origin/visibility/export/signature shell,
and validates provenance plus cross-index consistency. A local candidate
additionally requires a normal,
conflict-free `DefinitionEntry` of kind `Functor`, with matching
symbol/contribution/origin and matching notation when both indexes supply it,
whose declaration ends before the
use. An imported candidate requires public exported or re-exported provenance
from the imported contribution. Current resolver entries expose neither a
uniform application-use candidate API nor reliable parser-backed arity/fixity
(`DefinitionEntry::arity()` may legitimately be `None`). Therefore the public
producer neither parses opaque notation to infer those facts nor claims that a
reference is applicable to the supplied form/arity. The exact private real
selectors separately assert their frozen source head/form and selected
resolver identity. Task 278 owns use-site candidate collection, form/arity
relevance, viability, ranking, and winner authentication.
`Symbolic` applications have at least one
nonduplicate candidate reference in supplied `SymbolId` order. `Inline`
applications have none. Task 253 neither calls a winner-selection API nor
claims candidate completeness, applicability, viability, ranking, or
uniqueness.

Candidate origins must be non-recovered. A missing signature shell and
`SignatureShell::Pending` are accepted as unresolved request provenance;
`SignatureShell::Opaque` is accepted as opaque provenance only and never as a
semantic response. `SignatureShell::Malformed` and every recovered origin are
rejected.

`SourceFunctorTypeRequestKind` is `CandidateSignature` or
`ApplicationResultType`. Every symbolic candidate has exactly one
`CandidateSignature` request naming that candidate, followed by exactly one
application-level `ApplicationResultType` request whose candidate is `None`.
Request ordinals are dense within the application. Inline rows have no
candidate or type-request rows: Task 253 records only their generic source
application shape and ordered actuals. The requests are unresolved dependency
transport only. Task 253 has no response/result DTO and treats even an opaque
resolver signature shell as provenance, not a checker-semantic signature or
result type.

`SourceFunctorApplicationProducer::build(
SourceFunctorApplicationHandoffInput, &SymbolEnv, &BindingEnv,
&SourcePrimaryTermHandoff, &TypedArena
) -> Result<SourceFunctorApplicationHandoff,
SourceFunctorApplicationError>` authenticates all of the rules above and
publishes atomically. It never sorts, repairs, infers a candidate, chooses a
winner, resolves a type, or publishes partial output. `TypedAst` owns
`Option<SourceFunctorApplicationHandoff>` through a one-shot validated
installation, and `ResolvedTypedAst` only clone-preserves it. Raw `SurfaceAst`,
`SurfaceNodeId`, and syntax kinds remain in one private
`mizar-test::runner::type_elaboration::source_application` leaf. The leaf composes
the existing Task-252 producer for eligible actuals rather than duplicating
its extractor or public tables.

`TypedAst::validate_installation` requires the Task-252 handoff already
installed in that same `TypedAst`, compares its exact deterministic
`debug_text()` to `primary_term_fingerprint`, and revalidates every
`Primary(SourcePrimaryTermId)` target against it. Equal source/module IDs are
necessary but not sufficient. Any dependency-state change is rejected
atomically; an equivalent clone with identical debug text is accepted.
`ResolvedTypedAst` preservation revalidates the same association rather than
retargeting dense IDs.

## Task 254 Frozen Structure-Term Producer Contract

This section is the independent documentation prerequisite for Task 254. It
repairs the absent exact contract (`design_drift`) only. The public producer,
final checker handoff, exact real consumer, and producer/corruption/final-
ownership coverage remain `source_drift` and `test_gap` until a separate
implementation commit. Canonical Chapter 5 §§5.3-5.5 and 5.7 and Chapter 13
§13.3 are sufficient when read with the existing parser structure-expression
fixtures and resolver structure/selector projections; there is no blocking
`spec_gap`. MC-G017 and MC-G018 are the selected audit slices. Tasks 248-253
are dependencies, and the existing `mizar-test` Task-10 type-elaboration
runner is the exact consumer.

Task 254 must add one public, syntax-free `source_structure` module with seven
dense immutable tables. The exact transaction input is:

```text
SourceStructureHandoffInput {
    source_id: SourceId,
    module_id: ModuleId,
    terms: Vec<SourceStructureTermInput>,
    wrappers: Vec<SourceStructureWrapperInput>,
    roots: Vec<SourceStructureRootInput>,
    members: Vec<SourceStructureMemberInput>,
    field_updates: Vec<SourceFieldUpdateInput>,
    edges: Vec<SourceStructureEdgeInput>,
    requests: Vec<SourceStructureRequestInput>,
}
SourceStructureTermInput {
    site: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    source_ordinal: usize,
    context: BindingContextId,
    recovery: SourceStructureRecovery,
    spelling: String,
    kind: SourceStructureTermKind,
}
SourceStructureWrapperInput {
    term: SourceStructureTermId,
    ordinal: usize,
    site: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    context: BindingContextId,
    spelling: String,
    recovery: SourceStructureRecovery,
}
SourceStructureRootInput {
    term: SourceStructureTermId,
    symbol: SymbolId,
    contribution: SourceContributionId,
}
SourceStructureMemberInput {
    term: SourceStructureTermId,
    ordinal: usize,
    site: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    spelling: String,
    role: SourceStructureMemberRole,
    parent: Option<SourceStructureMemberId>,
}
SourceFieldUpdateInput {
    term: SourceStructureTermId,
    ordinal: usize,
    site: TypedSiteRef,
    source_range: SourceRange,
    spelling: String,
    first_member: SourceStructureMemberId,
    final_member: SourceStructureMemberId,
}
SourceStructureEdgeInput {
    term: SourceStructureTermId,
    ordinal: usize,
    role: SourceStructureEdgeRole,
    member: Option<SourceStructureMemberId>,
    target: SourceStructureTarget,
}
SourceStructureRequestInput {
    term: SourceStructureTermId,
    member: Option<SourceStructureMemberId>,
    request_ordinal: usize,
    kind: SourceStructureRequestKind,
}
```

`SourceStructureTermId`, `SourceStructureWrapperId`,
`SourceStructureRootId`, `SourceStructureMemberId`,
`SourceFieldUpdateId`, `SourceStructureEdgeId`, and
`SourceStructureRequestId` are dense zero-based row indices with public
`new(index)` and `index()` accessors. The immutable output has exact private fields
`SourceStructureHandoff { source_id, module_id,
primary_term_fingerprint, application_fingerprint: Option<String>, terms, wrappers, roots,
members, field_updates, edges, requests }`. There is one table and one read-only row type per
input vector. Every table exposes only `get(id)`, source-ordered `iter()`,
`len()`, and `is_empty()`; the handoff exposes source/module/fingerprint/table
accessors and deterministic `debug_text()`. There are no mutable or unchecked
public constructors. `SourceStructureProducer` validates the entire
transaction before publication. All public enums and the atomic
`SourceStructureError` are `#[non_exhaustive]`.

`SourceStructureTermKind` is exactly `Constructor`, `SelectorAccess`, or
`FunctionalUpdate`. `SourceStructureRecovery` is `Normal` or `Degraded`.
Term rows are source-preorder ordered and
`source_ordinal == SourceStructureTermId::index()`: an outer selector/update
precedes its structure-valued base, and an outer constructor precedes a
nested structure-valued assignment. Every row uses a unique
`TypedSiteRef::Node`, an exact source anchor, an existing Task-248 binding
context, and the typed kind key
`source.term.structure.constructor`, `source.term.structure.selector`, or
`source.term.structure.update`. Normal/degraded input must match the arena
recovery state. Spelling is the private extractor's deterministic token
spelling with tokens separated by one ASCII space.

A constructor has exactly one `SourceStructureRoot` and no other term kind
has one. The root row is an individually authenticated resolver
`SymbolKind::Structure` reference, not a structure-signature response. The
producer finds the exact `SymbolEntry` and `SourceContribution`, requires the
entry contribution to equal the supplied contribution, requires
`entry.kind() == SymbolKind::Structure`, requires the entry namespace to equal
the current module path, requires the contribution module to equal the
symbol's module, and requires the contribution effects to contain that exact
symbol. It clones the entry's `SemanticOrigin`, `Visibility`, `ExportStatus`,
and optional `SignatureShell`.

A local root requires `ContributionKind::LocalSource` for the current
source/module, a symbol and normal origin in that module with no import edge,
and an origin range that is valid and ends no later than the constructor use.
The symbol cross-indexes to exactly one normal, conflict-free
`DefinitionEntry` of kind `Structure`; definition symbol, contribution,
origin, visibility, and signature shell agree exactly with the `SymbolEntry`,
and the contribution effects contain that definition ID. An imported root
requires `ContributionKind::ImportedSource` for the current source, a valid
source-preceding contribution range, public exported or re-exported entry
provenance, an origin module equal to the symbol module, and an authenticated
import effect whose imported module is that same symbol module. Summary,
builtin, and every other contribution kind are rejected. Recovered origins,
malformed signature shells, stale or cross-index-inconsistent
symbol/definition/contribution records, and mismatched source/module/import
edges are rejected. Missing, pending, or opaque shells remain unresolved
provenance and never become field coverage, result type, or evidence.

The resolver currently projects both structure fields and structure
properties as `SymbolKind::Selector` declarations and intentionally defers
use-site dotted selection until the base type is known. It does not expose a
complete constructor-root-to-member or inheritance-view association. Task
254 therefore authenticates the constructor root but preserves every written
member occurrence as a source member row and unresolved request key. It must
not guess a selector `SymbolId`, treat equal spelling as ownership, or turn a
resolver declaration shell into a complete structure signature. This is the
exact resolver-provenance boundary. The private extractor proves the source
shape and member spelling; later Task 263 supplies structure-definition,
field/property, root declaration, and path/view payloads.

`SourceStructureMemberRole` is exactly `ConstructorAssignment`,
`Selector`, or `UpdatePathSegment`. A constructor member is one direct
`FieldArgument` label; a selector member is the identifier owned by one
`SelectorAccess`; and an update-path member is one identifier segment written
inside one parser `FieldUpdate`. `spelling` is a nonempty identifier. Every
member site is a distinct `TypedSiteRef::Node` whose arena kind is exactly
`source.term.structure.member.constructor-assignment`,
`source.term.structure.member.selector`, or
`source.term.structure.member.update-path-segment` according to its role; its
arena range is the exact identifier range recorded by the row. Member rows
are grouped by term, use dense per-term ordinals, retain source order, and
have nonempty nonoverlapping identifier ranges. Constructor and selector
members have no parent. Update-path segments form one or more source-ordered
chains: a chain root has no parent, each later segment names the immediately
preceding segment of the same term, and no segment has more than one child. A
path such as `start.x` therefore publishes two member rows with one parent
edge; it is not flattened to `"start.x"`.

The parser `FieldUpdate` node is an association container, not a term.
Each source node receives one `SourceFieldUpdateId` and preserves its site,
whole range, canonical spelling, dense per-update ordinal, first/final member,
and enclosing `FunctionalUpdate` term. Its site is a distinct
`TypedSiteRef::Node` with arena kind
`source.term.structure.field-update` and the exact whole `FieldUpdate` range.
It owns exactly one nonempty member path and one replacement-value edge, but
receives no
`SourceStructureTermId` of its own, wrapper, result-type request, independent
type, fact, axiom, or FOL node. The enclosing `StructureUpdate` is the sole
`FunctionalUpdate` term owner. Empty update lists, detached `FieldUpdate`
rows, multiply owned path segments, cross-update member chains, wrong
first/final member endpoints, and partial replacement edges are rejected
atomically. Repeated constructor labels and repeated update paths are
preserved in source order rather than accepted, rejected, or deduplicated:
Task 263 must decide them from authenticated member/coverage payloads. This
freezes the `FieldUpdate` ownership boundary without deciding whether two
differently written paths denote the same semantic root/member/view.

`SourceStructureEdgeRole` is exactly `ConstructorValue`, `SelectorBase`,
`SelectorArgument`, `UpdateBase`, or `UpdateValue`.
`SourceStructureTarget` is exactly
`Primary(SourcePrimaryTermId)`,
`Application(SourceFunctorApplicationId)`, or
`Structure(SourceStructureTermId)`. Constructor-value and update-value edges
name their associated final member; base and selector-argument edges have no
member. A constructor has one value edge per assignment. A selector has one
base followed by zero or more argument edges. A functional update has one
base followed by one replacement edge per `FieldUpdate` path. Per-term edge
ordinals are dense in that order.

A primary target must be a Task-252 root row in the same context. An
application target must exist as a root row in the optional Task-253 handoff,
must have the same binding context as the owning Task-254 term, and uses its
effective outer-wrapper range/spelling. A Task-253 application is a root for
this purpose exactly when no Task-253 argument edge targets that application;
transparent Task-253 wrappers do not change root status. A nested Task-253
application already has its Task-253 parent and is rejected rather than
multiply owned across families. A structure target names a later Task-254
preorder row in the same context and uses its own effective outer-wrapper
range/spelling. Every child target range is strictly contained by the owning
term, siblings are source ordered and nonoverlapping where the grammar
requires it, and every nested structure target has exactly one incoming edge.
Task 254 never copies a Task-252 primary row or Task-253 application row.

The edge table is exhaustive for the direct written partition of every
Task-254 term. Its candidates are parentless same-context Task-252 roots not
already owned by a Task-253 argument, same-context Task-253 root applications,
and later same-context Task-254 terms. A candidate contained by another
candidate is owned by that nearer child, not detached into the outer term.
After that filtering, the source-ordered candidates must equal the edge
targets exactly; omission, duplication, and retargeting fail atomically.
Constructor values occur after their assignment member and before the next
member, selector bases occur before the selector member and selector
arguments after it, update bases occur before the first `FieldUpdate`, and
each replacement occurs inside its owning `FieldUpdate` after the final path
member. The exact `FieldUpdate` spelling is the ` . `-joined member path,
` := `, and the effective target spelling.

This initial composition is deliberately one-way. Task-254 terms may consume
Task-252 primary and Task-253 application children, and may recursively
consume Task-254 structure children. The frozen Task-253 handoff still excludes
an application whose argument subtree contains a structure term, because its
already-published argument-target vocabulary cannot be retargeted atomically
without a separately frozen composition transaction. Task 254 does not reopen
Task 253 or duplicate that application. Such reverse-parent subtrees remain
whole-subtree excluded and receive no detached Task-254 descendants.

A `SourceStructureWrapper` owns transparent parentheses around one
structure-family term. Wrapper ordinals are outer-to-inner, contexts match,
ranges strictly nest, and every site is a distinct `TypedSiteRef::Node` with
arena kind `source.term.structure.parenthesized` and the exact wrapper range.
Canonical spelling recursively follows
`format!("( {} )", contained_spelling)`. A wrapper creates no primary term,
semantic term/type, fact, axiom, or FOL node. Parentheses enclosing a Task-254
term are not Task-252 rows and are not Task-253 wrappers.

`SourceStructureRequestKind` is exactly `ConstructorSignature`,
`MemberIdentity`, `InheritancePath`, or `ResultType`. Every constructor has
one application-level `ConstructorSignature` request naming no member. Every
member has one `MemberIdentity` request followed by one `InheritancePath`
request naming that member. Every term ends with one application-level
`ResultType` request. Request ordinals are dense within the term in that
order. These requests preserve the missing root/member/view and result-type
dependency identities only. There is no response/result DTO. In particular:

- a constructor assignment is not accepted as a declared field and no
  default, missing-field, type, order-normalization, or complete-coverage
  decision is made;
- a property-spelled constructor assignment is never accepted as a field;
  the Task-35 fields-only rule is enforced only when Task 263 supplies the
  authenticated member kind;
- a selector is not bound to a field/property or assigned a signature/result;
- an update path is not resolved through inheritance, and no immutable copy
  result is fabricated;
- no inheritance path, reduct view, upcast, evidence, constructor witness, or
  exact-instance fact is selected or created.

`SourceStructureProducer::build(
SourceStructureHandoffInput, &SymbolEnv, &BindingEnv,
&SourcePrimaryTermHandoff, Option<&SourceFunctorApplicationHandoff>,
&TypedArena
) -> Result<SourceStructureHandoff, SourceStructureError>` authenticates all
rules above and publishes atomically. The output derives
`primary_term_fingerprint` from the exact Task-252 `debug_text()` and derives
`application_fingerprint` from the optional Task-253 `debug_text()`. The
application fingerprint is `Some` exactly when at least one edge has an
`Application` target and is `None` otherwise. A previously installed but
unrelated Task-253 handoff may coexist with the `None` case; Task 254 neither
requires nor removes it. The producer never sorts, repairs, infers a member,
chooses a view, computes a result type, or publishes partial output.

`TypedAst` owns `Option<SourceStructureHandoff>` through one-shot
`with_source_structure`. Installation requires the Task-252 dependency
already installed, requires the Task-253 dependency exactly when an
application fingerprint is present, compares exact fingerprints, and
revalidates all referenced rows and cross-family ownership. Installing
Task 253 later through `with_source_application` also revalidates an existing
Task-254 handoff. Therefore a Task-253 argument cannot re-own a Task-254
primary target, and a Task-253 application cannot contain, partially overlap,
or bypass the closest Task-254 owner in either installation order. An
unrelated installed Task-253 handoff may coexist with an absent Task-254
application fingerprint only when its targets and ranges are disjoint from
Task 254. `ResolvedTypedAst` clone-preserves and revalidates the same
associations without rebuilding or retargeting dense IDs. Raw `SurfaceAst`,
`SurfaceNodeId`, `StructureConstructor`,
`SelectorAccess`, `StructureUpdate`, `FieldArgument`, and `FieldUpdate`
inspection remains in one private
`mizar-test::runner::type_elaboration::source_structure` leaf.
