### Public Syntax-Free Transaction

Implementation adds one public checker module, `source_set_term`, with six
dense immutable tables owned by one `SourceSetTermHandoff`:

| Table | Frozen contents |
| --- | --- |
| terms | one source occurrence with exact site/range and deterministic canonical token spelling, dense pre-order, outer Task-248 context, recovery, and `Enumeration`, `Comprehension`, `Choice`, or `Qua` kind |
| wrappers | transparent parentheses around one Task-255 occurrence, ordered outer-to-inner, with independent site/range/canonical-spelling/context/recovery |
| generators | one source-written `ComprehensionVariableSegment` declaration occurrence with comprehension owner, dense generator ordinal, identifier site/range/spelling, and exactly one target-type-site association |
| type sites | one term-owned or generator-owned bare target with expression/head sites and ranges, exact spelling/recovery, and `BuiltinSet` or `BuiltinObject` head |
| edges | ordered `EnumerationElement`, `ComprehensionMapper`, or `QuaBase` child association to one Task-252 primary, Task-253 root application, Task-254 root structure term, or Task-255 term |
| requests | dense term-local unresolved `ResultType`, generator-local `GeneratorSethood`, or term-local `ChoiceNonempty`/`QuaWidening` request |

The generated dense IDs are `SourceSetTermId`, `SourceSetWrapperId`,
`SourceSetGeneratorId`, `SourceSetTypeSiteId`, `SourceSetEdgeId`, and
`SourceSetRequestId`. `SourceSetTermHandoffInput` contains source/module
identity and six complete vectors. Its exact row inputs are:

- `SourceSetTermInput`: `site`, `source_range`, `source_ordinal`, `context`,
  `recovery`, `spelling`, and `kind`;
- `SourceSetWrapperInput`: `term`, wrapper `ordinal`, `site`, `source_range`,
  `context`, `recovery`, and deterministic canonical `spelling`;
- `SourceSetGeneratorInput`: owner `term`, generator `ordinal`, identifier
  `site`/`source_range`/`spelling`, outer `context`, `recovery`, and
  `type_site`;
- `SourceSetTypeSiteInput`: `owner`, expression
  `site`/`source_range`/`spelling`, head `head_site`/`head_range`/
  `head_spelling`, outer `context`, `recovery`, and `head`;
- `SourceSetEdgeInput`: owner `term`, edge `ordinal`, `role`, and `target`;
- `SourceSetRequestInput`: owner `term`, request `ordinal`, `kind`, optional
  `generator`, and optional `type_site`.

Those names abbreviate this exact public construction ABI:

```rust
pub struct SourceSetTermHandoffInput {
    pub source_id: SourceId,
    pub module_id: ModuleId,
    pub terms: Vec<SourceSetTermInput>,
    pub wrappers: Vec<SourceSetWrapperInput>,
    pub generators: Vec<SourceSetGeneratorInput>,
    pub type_sites: Vec<SourceSetTypeSiteInput>,
    pub edges: Vec<SourceSetEdgeInput>,
    pub requests: Vec<SourceSetRequestInput>,
}
pub struct SourceSetTermInput {
    pub site: TypedSiteRef,
    pub source_range: SourceRange,
    pub source_ordinal: usize,
    pub context: BindingContextId,
    pub recovery: SourceSetTermRecovery,
    pub spelling: String,
    pub kind: SourceSetTermKind,
}
pub struct SourceSetWrapperInput {
    pub term: SourceSetTermId,
    pub ordinal: usize,
    pub site: TypedSiteRef,
    pub source_range: SourceRange,
    pub context: BindingContextId,
    pub recovery: SourceSetTermRecovery,
    pub spelling: String,
}
pub struct SourceSetGeneratorInput {
    pub term: SourceSetTermId,
    pub ordinal: usize,
    pub site: TypedSiteRef,
    pub source_range: SourceRange,
    pub spelling: String,
    pub context: BindingContextId,
    pub recovery: SourceSetTermRecovery,
    pub type_site: SourceSetTypeSiteId,
}
pub struct SourceSetTypeSiteInput {
    pub owner: SourceSetTypeOwner,
    pub site: TypedSiteRef,
    pub source_range: SourceRange,
    pub spelling: String,
    pub head_site: TypedSiteRef,
    pub head_range: SourceRange,
    pub head_spelling: String,
    pub context: BindingContextId,
    pub recovery: SourceSetTermRecovery,
    pub head: SourceSetTypeHead,
}
pub struct SourceSetEdgeInput {
    pub term: SourceSetTermId,
    pub ordinal: usize,
    pub role: SourceSetEdgeRole,
    pub target: SourceSetTarget,
}
pub struct SourceSetRequestInput {
    pub term: SourceSetTermId,
    pub ordinal: usize,
    pub kind: SourceSetRequestKind,
    pub generator: Option<SourceSetGeneratorId>,
    pub type_site: Option<SourceSetTypeSiteId>,
}
```

Each of the six public dense IDs is a private-field newtype with
`pub const fn new(index: usize) -> Self` and
`pub const fn index(self) -> usize`. Each corresponding immutable table
exposes exactly `get(id) -> Option<&Row>`,
source-ordered `iter() -> impl Iterator<Item = (Id, &Row)>`,
`len() -> usize`, and `is_empty() -> bool`. The exact `(Table, Id, Row)`
substitutions are `(SourceSetTermTable, SourceSetTermId, SourceSetTerm)`,
`(SourceSetWrapperTable, SourceSetWrapperId, SourceSetWrapper)`,
`(SourceSetGeneratorTable, SourceSetGeneratorId, SourceSetGenerator)`,
`(SourceSetTypeSiteTable, SourceSetTypeSiteId, SourceSetTypeSite)`,
`(SourceSetEdgeTable, SourceSetEdgeId, SourceSetEdge)`, and
`(SourceSetRequestTable, SourceSetRequestId, SourceSetRequest)`.
The validated public rows expose these exact read-only accessors:

- term: `site() -> &TypedSiteRef`, `source_range() -> SourceRange`,
  `source_ordinal() -> usize`, `context() -> BindingContextId`,
  `recovery() -> SourceSetTermRecovery`, `spelling() -> &str`, and
  `kind() -> SourceSetTermKind`;
- wrapper: `term() -> SourceSetTermId`, `ordinal() -> usize`,
  `site() -> &TypedSiteRef`, `source_range() -> SourceRange`,
  `context() -> BindingContextId`, `recovery() -> SourceSetTermRecovery`,
  and `spelling() -> &str`;
- generator: `term() -> SourceSetTermId`, `ordinal() -> usize`,
  `site() -> &TypedSiteRef`, `source_range() -> SourceRange`,
  `spelling() -> &str`, `context() -> BindingContextId`,
  `recovery() -> SourceSetTermRecovery`, and
  `type_site() -> SourceSetTypeSiteId`;
- type site: `owner() -> SourceSetTypeOwner`, `site() -> &TypedSiteRef`,
  `source_range() -> SourceRange`, `spelling() -> &str`,
  `head_site() -> &TypedSiteRef`, `head_range() -> SourceRange`,
  `head_spelling() -> &str`, `context() -> BindingContextId`,
  `recovery() -> SourceSetTermRecovery`, and
  `head() -> SourceSetTypeHead`;
- edge: `term() -> SourceSetTermId`, `ordinal() -> usize`,
  `role() -> SourceSetEdgeRole`, and `target() -> SourceSetTarget`;
- request: `term() -> SourceSetTermId`, `ordinal() -> usize`,
  `kind() -> SourceSetRequestKind`,
  `generator() -> Option<SourceSetGeneratorId>`, and
  `type_site() -> Option<SourceSetTypeSiteId>`.

The frozen public enums are `SourceSetTermKind`, `SourceSetTermRecovery`,
`SourceSetTypeOwner`, `SourceSetTypeRole`, `SourceSetTypeHead`,
`SourceSetEdgeRole`, `SourceSetTarget`, and `SourceSetRequestKind`; every
public enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`. `SourceSetTypeOwner` is either
`Generator(SourceSetGeneratorId)` or
`Term { term: SourceSetTermId, role: SourceSetTypeRole }`, where the role is
`ChoiceTarget` or `QuaTarget`.
`SourceSetTarget` is exactly
`Primary(SourcePrimaryTermId)`,
`Application(SourceFunctorApplicationId)`,
`Structure(SourceStructureTermId)`, or
`SetTerm(SourceSetTermId)`.
`SourceSetTermRecovery` is exactly `Normal` or `Degraded`;
`SourceSetTypeHead` is exactly `BuiltinSet` or `BuiltinObject`;
`SourceSetEdgeRole` is exactly `EnumerationElement`,
`ComprehensionMapper`, or `QuaBase`; and `SourceSetRequestKind` is exactly
`ResultType`, `GeneratorSethood`, `ChoiceNonempty`, or `QuaWidening`.
`SourceSetTermError` is also a public atomic `#[non_exhaustive]` enum: every
validation failure aborts the complete transaction and no error variant
publishes a partial table.
The producer signature is exact:

```rust
impl SourceSetTermProducer {
    pub fn build(
        input: SourceSetTermHandoffInput,
        bindings: &BindingEnv,
        primary_terms: &SourcePrimaryTermHandoff,
        applications: Option<&SourceFunctorApplicationHandoff>,
        structures: Option<&SourceStructureHandoff>,
        arena: &TypedArena,
    ) -> Result<SourceSetTermHandoff, SourceSetTermError> {
        /* atomically validate and construct */
    }
}
```

The output ABI is exact:

```rust
pub struct SourceSetTermHandoff {
    source_id: SourceId,
    module_id: ModuleId,
    primary_term_fingerprint: String,
    application_fingerprint: Option<String>,
    structure_fingerprint: Option<String>,
    terms: SourceSetTermTable,
    wrappers: SourceSetWrapperTable,
    generators: SourceSetGeneratorTable,
    type_sites: SourceSetTypeSiteTable,
    edges: SourceSetEdgeTable,
    requests: SourceSetRequestTable,
}
```

It exposes `source_id() -> SourceId`, `module_id() -> &ModuleId`,
`primary_term_fingerprint() -> &str`,
`application_fingerprint() -> Option<&str>`,
`structure_fingerprint() -> Option<&str>`, one shared-reference accessor
named for each of the six tables, and deterministic `debug_text() -> String`.
The row and table fields are private. There is no public mutable accessor,
unchecked output constructor, or publication path other than
`SourceSetTermProducer::build`.

Per-kind cardinality is exact. An enumeration owns no generator or type site,
zero or more `EnumerationElement` edges, and one final `ResultType` request.
A comprehension owns one or more generators, exactly one bare type site and
one `GeneratorSethood` request per generator, exactly one
`ComprehensionMapper` edge, and one final `ResultType` request. A choice owns
no generator or edge, exactly one `ChoiceTarget` type site, one
`ChoiceNonempty` request associated with that site, and one final
`ResultType` request. A `qua` owns no generator, exactly one `QuaTarget` type
site, exactly one `QuaBase` edge, one `QuaWidening` request associated with
that site, and one final `ResultType` request. `GeneratorSethood` carries
exactly the generator ID and its exact type-site ID; `ChoiceNonempty` and
`QuaWidening` carry no generator and their owner term's exact type-site ID;
`ResultType` carries neither. Requests are dense within a term in written
dependency order, with `ResultType` last.

`spelling` is not a byte-exact source slice. The private extractor joins the
source tokens with one ASCII space and the producer authenticates the
following deterministic canonical spelling recursively:

- an enumeration is exactly `{ }` when it has no element edge and otherwise
  `{ ` plus the `EnumerationElement` target spellings joined by ` , ` plus
  ` }`;
- a comprehension is exactly `{ ` plus its sole `ComprehensionMapper` target
  spelling, ` where `, its generators in generator order joined by ` , `,
  and ` }`; each generator fragment is its canonical identifier spelling,
  ` is `, and its type-site spelling;
- a choice is exactly `the ` plus its `ChoiceTarget` type-site spelling;
- a `qua` term is exactly its `QuaBase` target spelling, ` qua `, and its
  `QuaTarget` type-site spelling;
- a wrapper is exactly `format!("( {} )", contained_spelling)`.

For an edge, target spelling means the target family's validated effective
spelling: the outermost family-owned wrapper spelling when one exists and
otherwise the targeted row spelling. The term row is the unparenthesized
concrete family node. Wrapper ordinals are dense outer-to-inner. Wrapper zero
is the outermost range; each following wrapper is strictly contained in its
predecessor; the final wrapper strictly contains the term range. Every
wrapper shares the term's context and must equal the canonical wrapper
formula around the next inner wrapper or the term. Missing, duplicated,
crossing, reversed, same-range, malformed-spelling, or cross-term wrapper
chains reject. Generator spelling must be one canonical lexer identifier. A
type site's expression spelling and `head_spelling` must both be exactly
`set` or `object` consistently with `SourceSetTypeHead`.

The API imports no parser/syntax type. It receives the complete transaction,
the Task-248 `BindingEnv`, Task-252 handoff, optional Task-253 and Task-254
handoffs, and `TypedArena`, authenticates every row, and either publishes all
six tables or publishes nothing. The output records the exact deterministic
Task-252 `debug_text()` as its primary fingerprint. Task-253 and Task-254
fingerprints are their exact deterministic `debug_text()` values and are
`Some` exactly when an edge targets that family; otherwise they remain
`None`, even when an unrelated handoff is installed. `TypedAst` owns the
result through one validated
installer; `ResolvedTypedAst` revalidates dependencies and clone-preserves
the immutable handoff without rebuilding or renumbering rows. Installation
must preserve unrelated optional Task-253/254 handoffs in either install
order. A targeted dependency must already be installed; missing or mismatched
target dependencies are rejected. Conversely, the Task-253 and Task-254
installers must revalidate an already installed Task-255 handoff before
accepting a later handoff.

The exact typed-arena vocabulary is frozen as four term keys
`source.term.set.enumeration`, `source.term.set.comprehension`,
`source.term.set.choice`, and `source.term.set.qua`, plus
`source.term.set.parenthesized`,
`source.term.set.comprehension-generator`, `source.term.set.target-type`, and
`source.term.set.target-type-head`. Cross-role or generic node-key
substitution is rejected. Each type site is deliberately a bare
Task-255-owned source target associated with either its term or generator,
not a fabricated Task-249 application:
`SourceTypeApplicationHandoff` remains bound one-to-one to Task-248
declarations. Argument-bearing, attributed, qualified, local/imported-symbol,
or otherwise non-bare target types are excluded whole-subtree in this initial
slice instead of being copied into a second type-expression graph.

A generator row preserves the written declaration occurrence only. It does
not allocate a checker `BindingId`, resolve mapper/condition references, or
claim capture. Task 257 owns the source-derived binder/context extension and
must key nested capture by resolved binding identity as Chapter 13 requires.
Until that handoff exists, any comprehension whose mapper, nested
comprehension, or condition refers to a generator is excluded whole-subtree.
Conditioned comprehensions are also excluded whole-subtree until Tasks
256-257 freeze the formula edge. Condition-free comprehensions whose mapper
does not refer to a generator are the bounded real slice. Multiple independent
generators and nested independent comprehensions remain synthetic shape
coverage.

An edge owns only parent/role/order identity. Task 252 retains primary
occurrence/binding/numeric-request ownership; Task 253 retains application
shape/candidates/arguments; Task 254 retains structure/member/update shape;
Task 255 retains its nested term row. A Task-253 target must be a root
application not targeted by another Task-253 argument. A Task-254 target must
be a root term not targeted by another Task-254 child edge. Reverse
Task-253/254 parents containing a Task-255 child remain whole-subtree excluded
because their frozen target vocabularies are not reopened. Every direct
written child is associated exactly once, in source order, with strict parent
containment and non-overlapping siblings. Partial publication, sorting,
repair, deduplication, or multiple ownership is forbidden.

The ownership partition is range- and ID-exact. For each written child slot,
the private extractor enumerates Task-252/253/254/255 effective occurrences
inside that slot. A primary effective range includes its eligible Task-252
transparent wrappers; application, structure, and Task-255 effective ranges
include only wrappers owned by their own family. Occurrences strictly
contained in another eligible occurrence in the same child slot are
descendants and are removed. The single remaining maximal occurrence must
cover the complete written child slot and becomes its edge target. Thus a
Task-252 primary already targeted by a Task-253 argument or Task-254 edge is
never also a Task-255 target; a Task-253 application already targeted by a
Task-254 edge is never also a Task-255 target; and descendants of a
Task-253, Task-254, or nested Task-255 child remain owned by that nearest
family. Zero maximal candidates, multiple incomparable candidates, partial
coverage, or a target already owned by another Task-255 edge reject the
complete transaction.

For fingerprint and install-order purposes, an unrelated Task-253/254 handoff
has no target ID and no effective occurrence whose range equals, contains, or
is contained by a Task-255 term, wrapper, or edge-target range. An installed
handoff that overlaps those ranges without the corresponding exact Task-255
target is not unrelated and is rejected. Public validation derives the same
partition from dependency rows, effective ranges, and authenticated arena
links; it does not trust the extractor's classification alone.

Requests are intents, never answers. One `ResultType` request ends each term.
Each generator adds one `GeneratorSethood` request; each choice adds one
`ChoiceNonempty` request; each `qua` adds one `QuaWidening` request. There are
no response, result, fact, coercion, obligation, normalized-type, reduct, or
accepted-evidence DTOs. These source-owner associations do not duplicate or
extend the Task-251 evidence handoff: converting them into
`SourceEvidenceRequestKind::Sethood`, `NonEmptiness`, `InheritancePath`, or
`CoercionViability` requests requires a separately frozen term-origin
extension. Choice stability/context normalization, witness
selection, sethood lookup, inheritance/cluster reachability, value/type
checking, and FOL encoding remain semantic owners outside Task 255.

### Public Syntax-Free Transaction

Implementation adds one public checker module, `source_atomic_formula`, with
eight dense immutable tables owned by one `SourceAtomicFormulaHandoff`:

| Table | Frozen contents |
| --- | --- |
| formulas | one atomic source occurrence with exact site/range, dense source ordinal, Task-248 context, recovery, canonical spelling, and predicate/equality/inequality/membership/type-assertion/attribute-assertion kind |
| wrappers | transparent parentheses around one Task-256 occurrence, ordered outer-to-inner, with independent site/range/spelling/context/recovery |
| predicate heads | the single non-negated, non-template ordinary predicate segment head, its left/right written arities, exact site/range/spelling, context, and recovery |
| candidates | one individually resolver-authenticated predicate symbol/contribution reference owned by a predicate head |
| type sites | one formula-owned bare asserted `set` or `object` type occurrence with expression/head sites, ranges, spellings, context, and recovery |
| attributes | one source-written, unqualified, argument-free assertion attribute with formula-local ordinal, exact target identity, resolver symbol/contribution, and positive or source-anchored `non` polarity |
| edges | every direct written formula-to-term association, ordered by source role, targeting exactly one Task-252 primary, Task-253 root application, Task-254 root structure term, or Task-255 root set term |
| requests | unresolved operand-expected-type, predicate-candidate-signature, type-assertion-reachability, or attribute-admissibility input intent with exact owner association |

The dense IDs are `SourceAtomicFormulaId`, `SourceAtomicWrapperId`,
`SourcePredicateHeadId`, `SourcePredicateCandidateId`,
`SourceAssertionTypeSiteId`, `SourceAssertionAttributeId`,
`SourceAtomicEdgeId`, and `SourceAtomicRequestId`.
`SourceAtomicFormulaHandoffInput` contains source/module identity and the
eight complete vectors. The exact flat row inputs are:

```rust
    pub target_spelling: String,
    pub context: BindingContextId,
    pub recovery: SourceAtomicFormulaRecovery,
    pub symbol: SymbolId,
    pub contribution: SourceContributionId,
    pub polarity: SourceAssertionAttributePolarityInput,
}
pub struct SourceAtomicEdgeInput {
    pub formula: SourceAtomicFormulaId,
    pub ordinal: usize,
    pub role: SourceAtomicEdgeRole,
    pub target: SourceAtomicTermTarget,
}
pub struct SourceAtomicRequestInput {
    pub formula: SourceAtomicFormulaId,
    pub ordinal: usize,
    pub kind: SourceAtomicRequestKind,
    pub edge: Option<SourceAtomicEdgeId>,
    pub candidate: Option<SourcePredicateCandidateId>,
    pub type_site: Option<SourceAssertionTypeSiteId>,
    pub attribute: Option<SourceAssertionAttributeId>,
}
```

`SourceAssertionAttributePolarityInput` is exactly `Positive` or
`Negative { non_site, non_range, non_spelling, non_recovery }`.
Every public enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`. The other exact frozen enums are:

- `SourceAtomicFormulaKind`: `PredicateApplication`, `Equality`,
  `Inequality`, `Membership`, `TypeAssertion`, or `AttributeAssertion`;
- `SourceAtomicFormulaRecovery`: `Normal` or `Degraded`;
- `SourceAssertionTypeHead`: `BuiltinSet` or `BuiltinObject`;
- `SourceAtomicEdgeRole`: `PredicateLeftArgument`,
  `PredicateRightArgument`, `BuiltinLeftOperand`,
  `BuiltinRightOperand`, or `AssertionSubject`;
- `SourceAtomicTermTarget`: `Primary(SourcePrimaryTermId)`,
  `Application(SourceFunctorApplicationId)`,
  `Structure(SourceStructureTermId)`, or
  `SetTerm(SourceSetTermId)`;
- `SourceAtomicRequestKind`: `OperandExpectedType`,
  `PredicateCandidateSignature`, `TypeAssertionReachability`, or
  `AttributeAdmissibility`.

Each dense ID is a private-field newtype with
`pub const fn new(index: usize) -> Self` and
`pub const fn index(self) -> usize`. Each immutable table exposes exactly
`get`, source-ordered `iter`, `len`, and `is_empty`. The validated rows expose
read-only accessors corresponding one-for-one to their input fields. Nested
negative polarity exposes its four source fields by shared reference/value as
appropriate. Input vectors, row fields, and output table storage remain
private after validation; there is no unchecked or mutable publication path.

The producer signature is exact:


The output is exact:


It exposes source/module identity, the four fingerprint accessors, one
shared-reference accessor for each table, and deterministic
`debug_text() -> String`. The Task-252 fingerprint is its exact
`debug_text()`. Task-253/254/255 fingerprints are `Some` exactly when an edge
targets that family and otherwise `None`, even when a range-disjoint
unrelated handoff is installed. `SourceAtomicFormulaError` is a public
atomic `#[non_exhaustive]` enum; any validation failure publishes nothing.

`TypedAst` has a one-shot validated `with_source_atomic_formula` installer

Installing a range-disjoint unrelated optional handoff either before or after

already installed Task-256 handoff and reject a missing, overlapping,
substituted, or fingerprint-mismatched target transaction.

### Shape, Cardinality, Spelling, And Ownership

Per-kind cardinality is exact:

- an ordinary predicate application owns exactly one head, at least one
  candidate, one or more left/right argument edges matching the head arities,
  no type site or attribute, and one `PredicateCandidateSignature` request per
  candidate;
- equality and inequality each own exactly two edges, left then right, and
  exactly two `OperandExpectedType` requests, each associated with its matching
  edge;
- membership owns exactly two edges, left then right, and exactly one
  `OperandExpectedType` request associated only with the right/container edge;
- a type assertion owns exactly one `AssertionSubject` edge, exactly one bare
  asserted type site, and exactly one `TypeAssertionReachability` request
  associated with that type site;
- an attribute assertion owns exactly one `AssertionSubject` edge, one or
  more attributes in written order, and exactly one
  `AttributeAdmissibility` request per attribute;
- wrappers never add a semantic formula, edge, request, type site, attribute,
  candidate, result, fact, or truth.

Requests are dense within each formula in dependency order. Candidate
signature requests follow candidate order; operand requests follow edge
order; assertion requests follow the type site or attribute order. Every
unused association field is `None`; every required association field is the
exact owner row. There is no result/truth request because this transaction
does not promise a truth-producing upstream service.

Canonical spelling is token-normalized, not a byte slice. Tokens are joined
with one ASCII space and then authenticated structurally:

- equality, inequality, and membership are
  `<left> = <right>`, `<left> <> <right>`, and
  `<left> in <right>`;
- a predicate is its left target spellings joined by ` , `, then the head
  spelling, then right target spellings joined by ` , `, with exactly one
  separating space between nonempty components;
- a type assertion is `<subject> is <type-site>`;
- an attribute assertion is `<subject> is ` plus attributes in order,
  separated by one space, where a negative occurrence is
  `non <target-spelling>`;
- a wrapper is exactly `format!("( {} )", contained_spelling)`.

The term spelling for an edge is the target family's validated effective
spelling, including its outermost family-owned transparent wrapper when
present. Formula wrapper ordinals are dense outer-to-inner, ranges are
strictly nested, every wrapper shares its formula context, and the innermost
wrapper strictly contains the formula. Missing, duplicate, crossing,
same-range, reversed, cross-formula, malformed, or noncanonical wrapper
chains reject the whole transaction.

The exact typed-arena keys are
`source.formula.atomic.predicate`,
`source.formula.atomic.equality`,
`source.formula.atomic.inequality`,
`source.formula.atomic.membership`,
`source.formula.atomic.type-assertion`,
`source.formula.atomic.attribute-assertion`,
`source.formula.atomic.parenthesized`,
`source.formula.atomic.predicate-head`,
`source.formula.atomic.asserted-type`,
`source.formula.atomic.asserted-type-head`,
`source.formula.atomic.attribute`,
`source.formula.atomic.attribute-target`, and
`source.formula.atomic.attribute-non`. Normal/degraded recovery, source
identity, context, range, arena key, and site uniqueness are validated for
every owned occurrence. Cross-role or generic-key substitution rejects.

Predicate candidates are individual references, not an exhaustive overload
set. The producer authenticates each symbol/contribution against
`SymbolEnv`, its source/module provenance, `SymbolKind::Predicate`, visibility,
and the written head spelling. Candidate rows are dense and unique. It does
not infer a missing candidate, merge same-spelling entries, read a semantic
signature, test viability, choose a winner, or create a predicate fact.
Task 278 retains collection/viability/selection.

Assertion attributes use the same resolver provenance discipline but are
formula-owned occurrences, not aliases for Task-250 chains attached to
Task-249 declaration type expressions. The exact Task-256 slice admits
one or more simple, unqualified, argument-free attribute references and
preserves each written `non`. It does not duplicate Task-250 rows or extend
Task-251 evidence origins. Attribute qualification, prefix/parenthesized
actuals, and formula-level `is not` remain whole-subtree excluded from this
bounded increment.

The asserted type site is likewise formula-owned, not a fabricated
Task-249 declaration application. This bounded slice admits only bare
builtin `set` or `object`, with identical expression/head spelling. Local or
imported type heads, type arguments, attributed types, and nested type graphs
remain whole-subtree excluded. Existing semantic type-assertion pass coverage
and `TermFormulaChecker` reachability behavior receive no new source-transport
credit beyond the exact bare site.

Each formula edge owns only parent/role/order identity. Task 252 retains
primary occurrence/reference/numeric-request ownership; Task 253 retains
application shape/candidates/arguments; Task 254 retains structure shape;
Task 255 retains set/choice/`qua` shape. A Task-253 target must be a root
application not targeted by another Task-253 argument; Task-254 and Task-255
targets must be roots not targeted by their own family edges. Descendants
remain owned by the nearest term family and never become duplicate Task-256
edges.

For every direct formula term slot, the private extractor enumerates the
effective Task-252/253/254/255 occurrences, removes occurrences strictly
contained in another eligible occurrence, and requires one maximal occurrence
whose effective range covers the complete slot. Siblings must be ordered,
strictly contained by the formula, and nonoverlapping. Zero or multiple
maxima, partial coverage, duplicate target ownership, cross-context targets,
or an optional dependency overlapping a formula/wrapper/edge range without
the corresponding exact target rejects atomically. Public validation derives
the same ownership partition from rows, ranges, fingerprints, and arena links;
it never trusts the extractor's family label alone.

Predicate chains and segment-level `does not`/`do not` conceptually introduce
conjunction/negation and therefore remain whole-subtree excluded until Task
257. Inline predicate applications remain Task 270 closure/substitution
ownership. Template predicate actuals remain Task 277. Formula constants,
prefix negation, connectives, quantifiers, and formula-level `is not` remain
Task 257. A Task-255 comprehension condition cannot be reopened by Task 256:
conditioned comprehensions still require the joint Task-255/256/257 contract
and remain excluded.

### Public Syntax-Free Transaction

Task 257A adds a public `source_composite_formula` module. The input and
immutable handoff have exactly seven dense tables, in this order:

1. `formulas`: Task-257-owned composite/constant formula occurrences;
2. `wrappers`: transparent parenthesized formula occurrences;
3. `roots`: maximal formula roots not yet assigned to a semantic statement
   owner;
4. `binders`: quantified binder declarations and their checker binding/context
   identities;
5. `type_sites`: binder-owned written type expression/head occurrences;
6. `edges`: ordered source child associations;
7. `requests`: unresolved formula-semantics and binder-type input intents.

Each public input row has a checker-owned dense id after validation. Every
source-bearing row retains its `TypedSiteRef`, half-open `SourceRange`,
source/group ordinal, `BindingContextId`, recovery state, and canonical
token-normalized spelling as applicable. All public enums are
`#[non_exhaustive]`; downstream consumers use wildcard arms.

The dense ids are `SourceCompositeFormulaId`, `SourceFormulaWrapperId`,
`SourceFormulaRootId`, `SourceQuantifierBinderId`,
`SourceBinderTypeSiteId`, `SourceFormulaEdgeId`, and
`SourceFormulaRequestId`. Each is a private-field newtype with
`pub const fn new(index: usize) -> Self` and
`pub const fn index(self) -> usize`. The exact flat input ABI is:

```rust
pub struct SourceCompositeFormulaHandoffInput {
    pub source_id: SourceId,

}

    pub source_range: SourceRange,
    pub source_ordinal: usize,

}

}
pub struct SourceQuantifierBinderInput {
```

The exact enum variants are:

- `SourceCompositeFormulaKind`: `Implication`, `Universal`, `Negation`, or
  `Contradiction`;
- `SourceCompositeFormulaRecovery`: `Normal` or `Degraded`;
- `SourceFormulaRootOwnership`: only `UnassignedStatement` in this slice;
- `SourceBinderTypeHead`: only `BuiltinSet` in this slice;
- `SourceFormulaEdgeRole`: `ImplicationLeft`, `ImplicationRight`,
  `UniversalBody`, or `NegatedFormula`;
- `SourceFormulaRequestKind`: `ConnectiveSemantics`, `ConstantSemantics`,
  `QuantifierSemantics`, `BinderType`, or `NegationSemantics`.

Each immutable table exposes exactly `get`, source-ordered `iter`, `len`, and
`is_empty`; validated rows expose read-only accessors corresponding
one-for-one to their input fields. Input vectors, row fields, and table
storage remain private after validation. There is no unchecked or mutable
publication path.

The exact producer surface is:

```rust
impl SourceCompositeFormulaProducer {
    pub fn extend_bindings(
        input: &SourceCompositeFormulaHandoffInput,
        base_bindings: &BindingEnv,
        arena: &TypedArena,
    ) -> Result<BindingEnv, SourceCompositeFormulaError>;

    pub fn build(
        input: SourceCompositeFormulaHandoffInput,
        bindings: &BindingEnv,
        arena: &TypedArena,
    ) -> Result<SourceCompositeFormulaHandoff, SourceCompositeFormulaError>;
}
```

`extend_bindings` requires the exact normal Task-248 module shell for this
source/module, preserves it and all four diagnostics, and atomically returns
the frozen `2/1/4` environment. It does not consume or mutate the input or
base environment. `build` requires that exact returned environment and
clone-owns it in the handoff. The exact output layout is:

```rust

```

It exposes source/module identity, `binding_env()`, one shared-reference

`SourceCompositeFormulaError` is a public atomic `#[non_exhaustive]` enum;
any validation failure publishes neither an environment extension nor a
handoff. `BindingContextOwner` gains the exact
`SourceFormula { source_range: SourceRange }` variant so the body context is

The exact real aggregate is:

```text
formula/wrapper/root/binder/type-site/edge/request = 5/0/1/1/1/4/6
```

Formula ids are deterministic parent-before-child preorder. `spelling` is the
canonical normalized direct-token spelling for the represented surface node:

| Formula id | Kind | Context | Range | Spelling |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | implication | 0 | `52..113` | `implies` |
| 1 | contradiction | 0 | `52..65` | `contradiction` |
| 2 | universal | 0 | `74..113` | `for holds` |
| 3 | negation | 1 | `96..113` | `not` |
| 4 | contradiction | 1 | `100..113` | `contradiction` |

The one root row is ordinal 0 and points to formula 0. It is explicitly
`UnassignedStatement`: the row preserves a source formula root while granting
no theorem/statement owner, status, visibility, fact, proof, or acceptance.
Task 258 may later associate an authenticated statement owner without
rewriting Task-257A source identity.

The four ordered edges are:

| Edge id | Parent | Role | Child |
|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 0 | 0 | implication-left | 1 |
| 1 | 0 | implication-right | 2 |
| 2 | 2 | universal-body | 3 |
| 3 | 3 | negated-formula | 4 |

Every non-root formula has exactly one incoming edge and the root has none.
Implication has exactly left/right children; universal has exactly one body
and no restriction in this slice; negation has exactly one operand; constants
have none. Edges preserve source role rather than semantic truth. Parent
ranges properly contain child effective ranges. Normal same-context edges
retain one context; the universal body edge is the sole permitted transition
from parent context 0 to body context 1.

The wrappers table is empty for the real source. Task 257B1 later supersedes
the former bounded synthetic Task-257A wrapper admission by partitioning the
producer into two exact profiles that both require an empty wrapper table.
The public wrapper row/table shape remains reserved, but executable
`ParenthesizedFormula` occurrences, nesting, ordinals, and canonical spelling

The six exact requests are dense and grouped by formula preorder:

| Request id | Formula | Kind | Association |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | connective-semantics | implication |
| 1 | 1 | constant-semantics | premise contradiction |
| 2 | 2 | quantifier-semantics | universal |

### Validation, Atomicity, And Installation

The producer rejects source/module/environment mismatch; missing, duplicate,
or reordered dense rows; invalid sites/ranges/node keys; duplicate sites;
noncanonical spelling; recovery substitution; invalid root/edge/binder/type/
request associations; missing or multiple parents; cycles; partial trees;
wrong context transitions; stale binding ids/scopes/ordinals/type sites;
same-scope duplicate binder names; missing module-shell diagnostics; or any
table mutation. Construction and installation are atomic and one-shot.

The exact typed-arena vocabulary is frozen as:

```text
source.formula.composite.implication
source.formula.composite.universal
source.formula.composite.negation
source.formula.constant.contradiction
source.formula.parenthesized
source.formula.quantifier-binder
source.formula.binder-type
source.formula.binder-type-head
```

Generic, cross-role, or lower-family node-key substitution is rejected.
Formula rows are parent-before-child preorder, while edge/request groups are
owner order then role/ordinal order. Equal input produces equal handoffs and
byte-identical nonempty debug text. The exact positive test is a single full
literal `debug_text()` snapshot, not `contains` checks or comparison of two
equally incomplete renderings. In order it contains the
`source-composite-formula-debug-v1` header, module identity, the complete
embedded `binding-env-debug-v1` bytes for contexts 0/1, binding 0, and all
four diagnostic rows, then every formulas/wrappers/roots/binders/type-sites/
edges/requests section and row. The empty wrappers heading is retained.
Formula, binder, type-site, edge, request, range, context, spelling, identity,
association, and diagnostic fields appear in the same order as their frozen
tables. A separate exact legacy `TypedAst::debug_text()` snapshot without
Task 257A must remain byte-identical.

`TypedAst::with_source_composite_formula` is one-shot. It authenticates the
source/module, typed arena, exact extended `BindingEnv`, and every table before
publication. `ResolvedTypedAst::assemble` only clone-preserves the installed
handoff and revalidates it; it never rebuilds from source. Legacy ASTs without
Task-257A retain their exact debug output.

| equality occurrence | distinct direct child of the condition site, range `177..182`, spelling `3 = 4` |
| recovery | Task-255 condition and Task-256 formula both normal |
| lower profile | Task-252 `4/0/4`, Task-253 `1/0/1/2/2`, Task-255 `1/0/1/1/1/1/2`, Task-256 `1/0/0/0/0/0/0/2/2` |

The Task-255 handoff must already authenticate term/condition ownership,
colon and wrapper anchors, condition-subtree containment, lower-family
exclusion, and its Task-252/253 fingerprints. The Task-256 handoff must
already authenticate the equality site, context, range, spelling, normal
recovery, two ordered Task-252 operand edges, and two
`OperandExpectedType` requests. Task 256C1 then recognizes the inverse
overlap only when the set term has exactly the matching condition row and the
condition site's arena node directly lists the formula site's node as a
child. Equal range and spelling, normal recovery on both rows, the condition
row's reference to the currently overlapping set-term ID, equality kind, and
formula context equal to the enclosing set term's context are all mandatory.
The relation check is ID-independent;
term/condition/formula IDs are 0 only in this exact one-row consumer.

The condition row intentionally has no context field. Task 256C1 does not
invent one and does not change the Task-255 public schema. It derives the
condition's lexical context from its immutable owner term and compares that
existing value with the formula context. The future Task-257C2 association
still performs its separately frozen full cross-family profile and
association check.

### Internal Validation And Compatibility Boundary

Only the private Task-256 range-validation path may change. It may receive the
existing `TypedArena` and use a private predicate for the authenticated
direct-condition relation. For each formula/set occurrence pair, validation
keeps the existing rule:

1. disjoint ranges are dependency-neutral;
2. an atomic formula that properly contains a set term remains valid; and
3. every other overlap fails with the existing
   `SourceAtomicFormulaError::SetTermDependencyMismatch`, except the exact
   equality-condition relation frozen above.

The exception is not a general "set contains formula" rule. Copied or stale
handoffs, wrong term/condition IDs, wrong range, spelling, recovery, kind, or
context, a non-comprehension term, a non-direct descendant, a substituted
optional set validation context, an unrelated overlapping set, and any
partial/crossing/equal-range relation without the authenticated condition row
remain rejected. Ordinal 0 is part of the exact one-row consumer profile, not
a hard-coded relation predicate: an otherwise authorized future equality
condition remains ID/ordinal-independent. Predicate application,
inequality, membership, assertions, composite/connective/quantified formulas,
multiple or nested conditions, and generator-dependent conditions are not
promoted by this task.

`SourceAtomicFormulaProducer::build` and
`SourceAtomicFormulaHandoff::validate_installation` retain their public and
crate-visible signatures. `SourceAtomicFormulaHandoffInput`, all nine public
tables, IDs, accessors, enums, `debug_text()`, and
`SourceAtomicFormulaError` are byte/API-identical. In particular,
`set_term_fingerprint()` remains `None` because the equality has no
Task-255-targeted edge. Building the atomic handoff with or without the
optional authenticated set-term handoff must produce equal handoffs and
byte-identical debug output. The set handoff is validation context, not a
published dependency.

No `TypedAst` production edit is planned. Its existing symmetric
transactions define the two required orders:

1. install Task 255, then Task 256; and
2. install Task 256 without the optional set handoff, then install Task 255,
   which revalidates the already installed atomic handoff.

Both orders must succeed after Task 256C1 and yield byte-identical immutable
atomic/set handoffs and full `TypedAst::debug_text()`. Failed invalid overlap
installation remains atomic through the existing
`InvalidSourceAtomicFormula` or `InvalidSourceSetTerm` variant, publishes
nothing, and permits a valid replay from the unchanged base object.
Resolved ownership and clone behavior do not change.

## Checker Task 257C3 Frozen Predicate-Chain Composition Contract

### Task, Authority, And Classification

Fresh post-Task-257C2 inventory selects Task 257C3 as the next
dependency-ready logical task. This documentation prerequisite freezes only
the syntax-free implicit-conjunction and segment-negation associations for
the already implemented Task-257C1 predicate-chain transport. It does not
reopen Task 252 or Task 256, create source-composite formula nodes, or grant
formula truth or result semantics.

Canonical authority is Chapter 9 §9.3.3 for deterministic adjacent predicate
splitting, Chapter 14 §§14.2-14.2.1 for the shared-boundary rule and
segment-local `does not` / `do not`, Chapter 14 §§14.3.1 and 14.3.5 for
conjunction and negation shape, and Chapter 14 §§14.7.1 and 14.7.3 for the
corresponding logical encoding. The existing
`pass_type_elaboration_formula_predicate_chain_segment_payload_001.miz`,
its sidecar, the Task-257C1 covered trace row, parser tests
`parser_recovers_missing_user_predicate_chain_term` and
`parser_rejects_mixed_user_and_builtin_predicate_chain`, and the committed
Task-252/256/257C1 public APIs are the executable authority. Tasks 257A/B and
257C2 provide only the established final-ownership and reciprocal-exclusion
pattern.

The absent composition contract is `design_drift`; its absent syntax-free
producer and exact consumer are bounded `source_drift` and `test_gap`.
There is no blocking `spec_gap`, `source_undocumented_behavior`,
`test_expectation_drift`, or `boundary_violation`. Origin divergence remains
a report-only `repo_metadata_conflict`; the task-only commit target remains
identifiable.

### Exact Consumer, Lower Profiles, And Exclusions

The complete Task-257C3 route runs before the lower Task-257C1 atomic-only

```text
source-predicate-chain-composition-debug-v1
```

Validation reauthenticates the source/module, nonempty exact Task-252 and
Task-256 fingerprints, both lower installations against the supplied arena,
the complete lower profiles, normal context/recovery, positive segment 0,
negative segment 1 with exact normal `does`/`not` tokens, dense source order,
the same imported symbol/contribution, and the canonical joined root
spelling. Conjunction 0 must associate formula 0, segments 0 and 1, and the
single Task-256 boundary edge 1. That edge must be segment 0's right edge and
segment 1's left edge, have role `PredicateChainBoundary`, and target
Task-252 primary 1. Negation 0 must associate only segment 1. Missing,
duplicate, copied, substituted, stale, cross-formula, wrong-edge,
wrong-polarity, wrong-token, wrong-profile, or extra rows fail before
publication. The producer checks both table cardinalities before validating
either row: a conjunction or negation cardinality other than exactly one
always yields `InvalidAggregate`. Only after both cardinalities are exactly
`1/1` does it validate conjunction 0 and then negation 0, yielding the
corresponding strongly typed row-local error. Because the profile contains
exactly one row in each table, ordinal and association swaps are row-local
invalid variants rather than an independent reordered-row aggregate case.

### Ownership, Tests, Audit Impact, And Exit

`TypedAst` and `ResolvedTypedAst` gain one optional
`SourcePredicateChainCompositionHandoff`, accessor, deterministic debug
projection, revalidation, and dedicated
`InvalidSourcePredicateChainComposition` error. Installation is one-shot and
requires the exact Task-252 and Task-256 handoffs first. It is reciprocally
exclusive with Task-257A composite ownership, Task-257B composition, and
Task-257C2 condition composition in every installation order. Failure leaves
byte-identical state and valid replay; resolved assembly clone-preserves the
handoff.

The six directional exclusion paths use the error owned by the installer
being attempted. Installing Task 257C3 after Task 257A, 257B, or 257C2 fails
with `TypedAstError::InvalidSourcePredicateChainComposition`. Installing
Task 257A, 257B, or 257C2 after Task 257C3 fails respectively with
`TypedAstError::InvalidSourceCompositeFormula`,
`TypedAstError::InvalidSourceFormulaComposition`, or
`TypedAstError::InvalidSourceConditionFormulaComposition`. Every path is an
atomic transaction: it publishes no field, preserves byte-identical state,
and permits a valid replay from the unchanged value.

## Task 258A Frozen-Contract Addendum

Fresh post-Task-257C3 inventory selects the first bounded Task-258 slice.
Task 258A freezes only the theorem-owner and source-statement boundary for
the future `MT10-FS` smoke source:

```mizar
reserve x for set;
theorem FormulaStatementReservedVariableEqualitySmoke: x = x;
```

The exact source is 81 bytes including its final LF and has SHA-256
`341aad596ef6891dfa33c189895df2350d357ac8edaf3747f160bbad7a2ddd96`.
Ranges are reserve `0..18`, written `set` `14..17`, theorem/owner `19..80`,
label `27..72`, equality `74..79`, left `x` `74..75`, `=` `76..77`, and
right `x` `78..79`.

Authority is Chapter 4 §§4.3/4.7.1, Chapter 14 §14.5.2, Chapter 15
§§15.8/15.10, and Chapter 16 §§16.1/16.2/16.7.1/16.9. The free reserved
identifier is implicitly universally closed with its reserved `set` type;
the theorem has a mandatory resolver identity; and an omitted justification
on an unmodified theorem is only automatic-proof intent, not acceptance.
The complete canonical component contract is
[source_statement.md](./source_statement.md).

### Authority slice, exact consumers, and lower profiles

The later private `mizar-test` route parses and resolves the exact 81-byte
source through the real frontend and invokes one syntax-free transaction. It
does not add the `.miz` or sidecar yet. That future corpus artifact remains
owned by `MT10-FS`; the current implementation tests use the exact source
through the library frontend/resolver path and leave all active corpus cases
unchanged.

The transaction consumes a Task-48-derived normal module `BindingEnv` with
one active visible reserved binding 0 for `x`, Task-252 `2/2/0`, Task-256
`1/0/0/0/0/0/2/2`, and their shared arena. Task 248 supplies the binding
model but its current exact `SourceBindingContextHandoff` profiles cannot
represent reserve plus theorem and are absent. Task 249, Tasks 253-255, and
every Task-257 owner are absent. The two Task-252 references have exact
stored use ordinals 1 and 1. The runner's separate upstream binding/use
source-event lookup ordinals are left/right 1 and 2.

The resolver has one and only one current-source theorem. Its
`SymbolEntry`, `DefinitionEntry`, `LabelEntry`, and
`CheckedStatementOwner::validate_exact_local_theorem` result agree on
the exact symbol, normal local theorem origin `19..80`, spelling,
contribution, `Theorem` kinds, `Public`
visibility, and `Exported` status. The module-wide `SourceContribution`
retains the real first-shell reserve anchor `0..18` and records the theorem
symbol, definition, and label effects. The runner's exact label
selector/projection range is `27..72`; the published label carries the
shared theorem origin and no separate declaration-range field. Imported,
summary, recovered, stale, duplicated, private, local-only, wrong-kind,
cross-contribution, or source/module-inconsistent owners fail closed.

The new public `source_statement` module has exactly five dense families:

```rust
SourceTheoremOwnerId / SourceTheoremOwnerInput / SourceTheoremOwnerTable
SourceStatementId / SourceStatementInput / SourceStatementTable
SourceStatementContextId / SourceStatementContextInput / SourceStatementContextTable
SourceStatementInputFactId / SourceStatementInputFactInput / SourceStatementInputFactTable
SourceStatementCandidateFactId / SourceStatementCandidateFactInput / SourceStatementCandidateFactTable
```

The complete input is `SourceStatementHandoffInput`; immutable output is
`SourceStatementHandoff`; construction is
`SourceStatementProducer::build`. The producer takes `&SymbolEnv`,
`&BindingEnv`, `&SourcePrimaryTermHandoff`,
`&SourceAtomicFormulaHandoff`, and `&TypedArena`, computes and stores the two
lower debug fingerprints, clones and stores the exact validated
`BindingEnv` plus its quoted debug fingerprint, authenticates every relation,
and publishes only after the full transaction validates. Dense IDs have
`new/index`; tables have only `get/iter/len/is_empty`; immutable rows have
read-only accessors; the handoff has source/module/binding-env/fingerprint/
checked-owner/table accessors and stable `debug_text()`. All public enums and errors are
`#[non_exhaustive]`.

The exact public enums admit only:

```rust
SourceTheoremRole::Theorem
SourceTheoremStatus::Unmodified
SourceStatementKind::TheoremProposition
SourceStatementRecovery::{Normal, Degraded}
SourceStatementFormulaTarget::Atomic(SourceAtomicFormulaId)
SourceStatementInputFactKind::ReservedTypeGuard
SourceStatementCandidateFactKind::UnverifiedProposition
```

The exact error variants are `DependencyMismatch`,
`InvalidOwner { owner }`, `InvalidStatement { statement }`,
`InvalidContext { context }`, `InvalidInputFact { fact }`,
`InvalidCandidateFact { fact }`, and `InvalidAggregate`.
All producer, installation, and final-assembly validation uses one total
precedence: the source/module, owned `BindingEnv`, exact Task-252/256
profiles and fingerprints, shared arena, and required lower installation
available to the entry point first (`DependencyMismatch`); all five
cardinalities and dense aggregate order second (`InvalidAggregate`); then
the first invalid owner, statement, context, input-fact, or candidate-fact
row in that order. Only the producer receives `SymbolEnv`; it validates live
resolver theorem identity and provenance in the owner tier and yields
`InvalidOwner`. Later entry points instead revalidate the stored
`CheckedStatementOwner` against owner row 0 and do not re-query resolver
views. Mixed dependency/cardinality corruption is dependency-first; mixed
aggregate/row corruption is aggregate-first.

### Frozen rows, ownership, and semantic boundary

The profile is `1/1/1/1/1`. Owner 0 is the resolver-authenticated theorem
label. Statement 0 spans `19..80`, is normal `TheoremProposition`, owns the
exact token spelling, and links owner/context 0 to
`Atomic(SourceAtomicFormulaId::new(0))`. Context 0 uses binding context 0 and
visible bindings exactly `[BindingId::new(0)]`. Input fact 0 is one
`ReservedTypeGuard` for binding 0 with exact Task-252 references `[0, 1]`.
Candidate fact 0 is one `UnverifiedProposition` for the same atomic equality.

The candidate is not visible input, type fact, checked formula,
`StatementSemantic`, checked proof, theorem result, axiom, accepted premise,
or discharged goal. The existing Task-266/268 standalone-contradiction path
retains exclusive ownership of checked statement/proof tables. Task 272
retains omitted-justification and proof-skeleton semantics.

installation/final clone, and dedicated `InvalidSourceStatement` errors.
Task-252/256 must be installed first. The chunk appears after all Task-257
formula-owner chunks and before the existing node/table output. Failed
installation publishes no field, preserves byte-identical state, and allows
valid replay. The handoff-owned environment makes binding provenance
revalidation implementable without changing either installer signature or
final-assembly inputs.

Task 248 and Task 258A are mutually exclusive. Production has only the

The exact route leaves typed facts, checked formulas, statement semantics,
checked proofs/nodes/goals, cluster facts, diagnostics, CoreIr,
ControlFlowIr, VC, cache, and artifacts empty. It adds no accepted-status or

The selector rejects every lemma/status/role variant, justification or proof
block, explicit assumption/conclusion/witness/citation, local label,
composite or other atomic formula, parentheses, multiple item, shadowed,
imported, definition, recovered, missing-final-LF, byte-different,

```rust

    input: SourceStatementHandoffInput,
```

`NamespacePath` and `SourceContributionId`, and
`resolved: &'a SurfaceResolvedArena`, then returns
`Result<Self, ProofLabelSourceCollectionError>`. `collect(&self)` returns
`Result<ProofLabelSourceCollection, ProofLabelSourceCollectionError>`;
`projections()` and `references()` are the collection accessors. Only `ast`
and `resolved` are borrowed/stored under the same `'a`; module is not stored,
while namespace and contribution are owned. The exact public non-exhaustive
error declaration is also canonical there: it wraps
`SurfaceResolvedArenaError`, and both overflow variants carry
`node: SurfaceNodeId`. Checked scope/path conversion has no unwrap,
saturation, truncation, or panic. Neither collector nor runner may create a
resolved-node id, scope component, or statement ordinal. R-032B later owns
exactly `crates/mizar-resolve/src/labels.rs`,
`crates/mizar-resolve/src/labels/tests.rs`, and
`crates/mizar-resolve/tests/lint_policy.rs`, where the last file may receive
only the R-026 owning-spec decision that maps
`ProofLabelSourceCollectionError` to `labels.md`.

Fresh implementation preflight classifies the earlier two-Rust-file R-032B
scope as High `design_drift`, not a semantic `spec_gap` or `test_gap`: the
mandatory R-026 guard necessarily scans the new public enum. Before R-032B
implementation, a separate synchronized docs-only correction freezes that
exact three-Rust-file scope across exactly 31 design files: eight paired
resolver families, four paired checker families, three paired `mizar-test`
families, and the global design TODO. It changes no production source, test

diagnostic code, semantic behavior, or coverage state.
`doc/design/spec_coverage_audit.md` is deliberately unchanged because no
mapping, owner, deferral, or coverage credit changes.

The exact upper route is `Root -> CompilationUnit -> ItemList`. Root has
exactly one normal CompilationUnit structural child, CompilationUnit has
exactly one normal ItemList, and ItemList scans direct normal TheoremItem
children while skipping/no-descending every other item child. Each such
direct normal `TheoremItem` with a direct `ProofBlock` is a supported proof
root, indexed in stable module source order as `[t]`;
supported nested proofs extend it as `[t, child, ...]` in direct proof-child
source order. Thus these one-theorem sources retain `[0]`, `[0,0]`,
`[0,1]`, and `[0,0,0]`. R-032B includes only an exact labelled
`CompactStatement`, the exact `JustificationClause -> ReferenceList ->
Reference` chain for a simple unqualified identifier under `by`, supported
nested proofs, and supported normal `CompactStatement` and
`ConclusionStatement` rows. Broader statement kinds, label forms,
qualified/grouped/bulk citations, indirect proof owners, non-theorem items,
and recovered or malformed nodes are excluded. Exclusion grants no checker
subtree ownership.

One module-global one-based ordinal counter spans every supported theorem
root and is never reset. A theorem owner consumes no ordinal. R-032B visits
supported normal `CompactStatement`/`ConclusionStatement` rows in
depth-first preorder through supported nested proofs; every such statement
consumes one ordinal, and a reference uses its owning statement's ordinal.
Transparent containers and unsupported/recovered/malformed/excluded
subtrees consume none and are not descended. A projection becomes visible
at the maximum ordinal in its whole labelled compact-statement subtree.
Thus inner B5C consumes `1..5`: A declares at 2, its own-proof statement is
3, completion is 3, the following same-block statement is 4, and the outer
reference's owning `ConclusionStatement` is 5. The sibling source consumes
`1..6`, with its reference owned by statement 6.

R-032B must collect exactly one `ProofStep`, `Private`/`LocalOnly`
projection for `A` with declaration scope `[0,0]`, visible only after
completion ordinal 3, contribution 0, and exact label-token provenance. It
must also collect exactly one unqualified `ProofOrTheorem` reference
candidate: node 52, ordinal 5, scope `[0]` for inner-to-outer; node 60,
ordinal 6, scope `[0,1]` for sibling. A same-block citation after completion
is the required positive boundary, while a reference from the label's own
proof is unresolved. Cross-theorem same-spelling labels neither conflict nor

### R-032B default-deny traversal and active provenance amendment

The canonical resolver traversal is an allowlist, not a generic syntax walk.
Its exact upper chain is
`Root -> CompilationUnit -> ItemList -> direct TheoremItem`: Root requires
exactly one normal CompilationUnit structural child; CompilationUnit
requires exactly one normal ItemList; and ItemList scans direct normal
TheoremItem children while skipping/no-descending all other item children.
Each admitted TheoremItem admits only its direct normal ProofBlock, which
admits only direct normal
`CompactStatement` and `ConclusionStatement` children. A
`CompactStatement` inspects only its proposition label. Both supported
statement kinds may descend only to their direct `ProofBlock` and
`JustificationClause` children. A citation is admitted only through the
exact `JustificationClause -> ReferenceList -> simple Reference -> sole
identifier token` chain. Formula children, tokens, wrappers, unsupported,
recovered, or malformed nodes, qualified/grouped/bulk citations, and
template forms are default-denied: they produce no projection or candidate,
consume no statement ordinal, and are not descended. R-032B tests exercise
every allowed edge, including each upper edge, positively. Upper negatives
cover missing/additional/wrong Root and CompilationUnit children, a theorem
relocated directly beneath Root or CompilationUnit, and a
`VisibleItem`-wrapped theorem. Lower negatives reject otherwise valid
children relocated beneath a forbidden parent or wrapper. Mixed-reference-list
tests collect only exact simple `Reference` siblings in source order and prove
that unsupported siblings add no row or descent.

The later active runner independently authenticates provenance after
source-byte-plus-normal-AST selection. It requires
`env.module_id() == resolver.module`, derives the expected namespace only as
`NamespacePath::new(module.path().as_str())`, and validates that every
collected projection uses that namespace. It acquires exactly one
contribution, requires id 0, `LocalSource`, record module equal to the
authenticated module, and LocalSource source id equal to the public
`ast.source_id` field. Every projection must repeat the authenticated
module, namespace, and contribution id.

The runner mutation matrix changes each of these independently: environment
module; projection module; projection namespace; projection contribution
id; contribution cardinality zero and multiple; contribution id;
contribution kind `ImportedSource`, `Summary`, and `Builtin`; contribution
record module; and contribution LocalSource source id. Every such mutation
emits only `declaration_symbol.label.proof_scope_input`, never
`declaration_symbol.label.proof_scope_confinement` or a public code. The
selector remains based only on frozen source bytes plus the exact normal AST;
copying or mutating expectations cannot select it. This refinement does not
change the exact 48-file documentation scope or any count, hash, trace, or
coverage state.
